R1-001.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-001.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-001.paraphrase: A trial should be conducted in compliance with the protocol that has received prior IRB/IEC approval or favourable opinion.
R1-001.quote: A trial should be conducted in compliance with the protocol

R1-002.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-002.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-002.paraphrase: Factors critical to the quality of the trial should be identified prospectively; quality by design means focusing on these critical to quality factors so the trial is likely to meet its objectives.
R1-002.quote: Factors critical to the quality of the trial should be identified prospectively.

R1-003.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-003.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-003.paraphrase: Strategies should be implemented to avoid, detect, address and prevent recurrence of serious noncompliance with GCP, the trial protocol and applicable regulatory requirements.
R1-003.quote: avoid, detect, address and prevent recurrence of serious noncompliance

R1-004.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-004.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-004.paraphrase: Trial processes should be proportionate to the risks inherent in the trial and to the importance of the information collected; risks cover participant rights, safety and well-being and the reliability of results.
R1-004.quote: Trial processes should be proportionate to the risks inherent in the trial

R1-005.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-005.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-005.paraphrase: Risks to critical to quality factors should be managed proactively and adjusted when new or unanticipated issues arise once the trial has begun.
R1-005.quote: Risks to critical to quality factors should be managed proactively

R1-006.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-006.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-006.paraphrase: Trial processes should be operationally feasible and avoid unnecessary complexity, procedures and data collection; the sponsor should not place unnecessary burden on participants and investigators.
R1-006.party: sponsor (for the burden clause; otherwise not named)

R1-007.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-007.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-007.paraphrase: The clinical trial protocol and the plans or documents for protocol execution (e.g. statistical analysis plan, data management plan, monitoring plan) should be clear, concise and operationally feasible.
R1-007.quote: should be clear, concise and operationally feasible
R1-007.record: protocol; statistical analysis plan; data management plan; monitoring plan

R1-008.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-008.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-008.paraphrase: Essential records should be retained securely by sponsors and investigators for the required period per applicable regulatory requirements and be available on request to regulatory authorities, monitors, auditors and IRBs/IECs (as appropriate).
R1-008.quote: Essential records should be retained securely by sponsors and investigators

R1-009.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-009.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-009.paraphrase: The sponsor may transfer, or the investigator may delegate, their activities, but they retain overall responsibility for their respective activities.
R1-009.quote: they retain overall responsibility for their respective activities

R1-010.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-010.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-010.paraphrase: Sponsors or investigators should maintain appropriate oversight of the activities they delegate or transfer.
R1-010.quote: should maintain appropriate oversight of the aforementioned activities

R1-011.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-011.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-011.paraphrase: The IRB/IEC's written procedures should specify that no deviation from or change to the protocol is initiated without prior documented IRB/IEC approval/favourable opinion of an appropriate amendment, except where necessary to eliminate immediate hazards to participants or where the change involves only logistical or administrative aspects, in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements.
R1-011.party: IRB/IEC (procedures; duty-holder of the rule not named)
R1-011.quote: no deviations from or changes to the protocol should be initiated

R1-012.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-012.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-012.paraphrase: The IRB/IEC's procedures should specify that the investigator/institution promptly reports to the IRB/IEC deviations from the protocol made to eliminate immediate hazards to trial participants (cross-references to 1.4.7, 2.5.4 and 2.5.5).
R1-012.quote: Deviations from the protocol to eliminate immediate hazards to the trial participants

R1-013.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-013.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-013.paraphrase: The IRB/IEC's procedures should specify that the investigator/institution promptly reports changes that increase the risk to participants and/or significantly affect the conduct of the trial (cross-reference to 2.4.6).
R1-013.quote: Changes increasing the risk to participants and/or significantly affecting the conduct of the trial

R1-015.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-015.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-015.paraphrase: The investigator retains ultimate responsibility and should maintain appropriate oversight of persons or parties undertaking delegated activities; the level of oversight should depend on the nature of the delegated activities and be proportionate to the importance of the data and the risks to participant safety and data reliability.
R1-015.quote: The investigator retains the ultimate responsibility

R1-016.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-016.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-016.paraphrase: The investigator or sponsor should promptly inform the IRB/IEC (see 1.4.8) and, where applicable, the institution of changes that significantly affect the conduct of the trial or increase the risk to participants.

R1-017.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-017.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-017.paraphrase: The investigator should comply with the protocol, GCP and applicable regulatory requirements.

R1-018.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-018.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-018.paraphrase: The investigator should document all protocol deviations.

R1-019.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-019.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-019.paraphrase: In addition to deviations identified by the investigator, protocol deviations relevant to the investigator's participants and their conduct of the trial may be communicated by the sponsor (cross-reference to 3.11.4.5.1(b)).

R1-020.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-020.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-020.paraphrase: In either case (investigator-identified or sponsor-communicated), the investigator should review the deviations and, for those deemed important, explain the deviation (cross-reference to 3.9.3).

R1-021.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-021.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-021.paraphrase: For important deviations the investigator should implement appropriate measures to prevent recurrence, where applicable.

R1-022.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-022.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-022.paraphrase: The investigator should follow the protocol and deviate only where necessary to eliminate an immediate hazard to trial participants.
R1-022.quote: deviate only where necessary to eliminate an immediate hazard(s)

R1-023.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-023.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-023.paraphrase: In case of a deviation undertaken to eliminate an immediate hazard, the investigator should inform the sponsor promptly.

R1-024.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-024.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-024.paraphrase: In the case of an immediate hazard, the investigator should report information on the immediate hazard, the implemented change and any subsequent proposed protocol amendment to the IRB/IEC and, where applicable, to regulatory authorities.
R1-024.quote: report information on the immediate hazard
R1-024.record: report on immediate hazard, implemented change and proposed amendment

R1-025.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-025.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-025.paraphrase: Source records should be attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original, accurate and complete; changes to source records should be traceable and explained if necessary.
R1-025.quote: Source records should be attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original, accurate and complete.

R1-026.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-026.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-026.paraphrase: Data reported to the sponsor should be consistent with source records or discrepancies explained; changes or corrections to reported data should be traceable and should not obscure the original entry.
R1-026.quote: Changes or corrections in the reported data should be traceable

R1-027.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-027.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-027.paraphrase: Trial records should be maintained as specified in Appendix C and applicable regulatory requirements; the investigator/institution should have control of all essential records it generates.
R1-027.quote: should have control of all essential records generated

R1-028.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-028.deadline: retention period per applicable regulatory requirements or sponsor notice, whichever is longest
R1-028.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-028.paraphrase: The investigator/institution should retain essential records for the retention period required by applicable regulatory requirements or until the sponsor informs them they are no longer needed, whichever is the longest, and take measures to ensure availability, accessibility and readability and to prevent unauthorised access and premature destruction (see Appendix C).

R1-030.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-030.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-030.paraphrase: In building quality into trial design, the sponsor should identify factors critical to the quality of the trial and manage risks to those factors.
R1-030.quote: factors that are critical to the quality of the trial

R1-031.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-031.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-031.paraphrase: The sponsor should ensure that trial processes are conducted in compliance with the protocol and related documents, applicable regulatory requirements and ethical standards.

R1-032.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-032.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-032.paraphrase: The sponsor should determine the necessary trial-specific criteria for classifying protocol deviations as important.
R1-032.quote: The sponsor should determine necessary trial-specific criteria for classifying protocol deviations as important.

R1-033.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-033.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-033.paraphrase: Important protocol deviations are a subset of protocol deviations that may significantly affect the completeness, accuracy and/or reliability of trial data or significantly affect a participant's rights, safety or well-being.
R1-033.party: not applicable (definition in sponsor oversight section)
R1-033.quote: Important protocol deviations are a subset of protocol deviations

R1-034.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-034.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-034.paraphrase: The range and extent of oversight measures should be fit for purpose and tailored to trial complexity and risks; selection and oversight of investigators and service providers are fundamental features, and oversight includes QA and QC of their trial-related activities.
R1-034.quote: The range and extent of oversight measures should be fit for purpose

R1-035.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-035.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-035.paraphrase: The sponsor should ensure appropriate and timely escalation and follow-up of issues so that appropriate actions can be taken.

R1-036.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-036.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-036.paraphrase: The sponsor should implement a system to manage quality throughout all stages of the trial, using a proportionate, risk-based approach that builds quality into design and identifies factors likely to have a meaningful impact on participant protection and reliability of results, i.e. critical to quality factors as described in ICH E8(R1).
R1-036.quote: critical to quality factors as described in ICH E8(R1)

R1-037.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-037.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-037.paraphrase: The sponsor should describe the quality management approach implemented in the trial in the clinical trial report (see ICH E3).

R1-038.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-038.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-038.paraphrase: The sponsor should identify risks that may have a meaningful impact on critical to quality factors, prior to trial initiation and throughout conduct, considering processes and systems including computerised systems (e.g. trial design, participant selection, informed consent, randomisation, blinding, investigational product administration, data handling, service provider activities).
R1-038.quote: identify risks that may have a meaningful impact on critical to quality factors

R1-039.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-039.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-039.paraphrase: The sponsor should evaluate identified risks and existing controls by considering the likelihood of harm/hazard occurring, the extent to which it would be detectable and its impact on participant protection and reliability of trial results.

R1-040.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-040.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-040.paraphrase: Risk control should be proportionate to the importance of the risk to participants' rights, safety and well-being and the reliability of trial results; risk mitigation may be incorporated e.g. in protocol design and implementation, monitoring plans, agreements defining roles and responsibilities, and training.
R1-040.record: risk control measures (e.g. in monitoring plan, protocol)

R1-041.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-041.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-041.paraphrase: Where relevant, the sponsor should set pre-specified acceptable ranges (e.g. quality tolerance limits at the trial level) to support the control of risks to critical to quality factors; the ranges reflect limits that, when exceeded, may impact participant safety or reliability of results.

R1-042.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-042.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-042.paraphrase: Where deviation beyond the pre-specified acceptable ranges is detected, an evaluation should be performed to determine whether there is a possible systemic issue and whether action is needed.
R1-042.quote: an evaluation should be performed to determine if there is a possible systemic issue

R1-043.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-043.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-043.paraphrase: The sponsor should document identified risks and mitigating activities and communicate them to those who are involved in taking action or are affected; communication supports risk review and improvement.

R1-044.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-044.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-044.paraphrase: The sponsor should periodically review risk control measures to ascertain whether the implemented quality management activities remain effective and relevant, taking into account emerging knowledge and experience; additional risk control measures may be implemented as needed.

R1-045.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-045.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-045.paraphrase: The sponsor should summarise and report important quality issues (including instances in which acceptable ranges are exceeded, see 3.10.1.3) and the remedial actions taken, and document them in the clinical trial report (see ICH E3).
R1-045.quote: document them in the clinical trial report (see ICH E3)

R1-047.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-047.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-047.paraphrase: Quality control should be applied using a risk-based approach at each stage of data handling; monitoring and data management are the main QC activities, which can extend to facilities outside investigator sites (e.g. central image reading).

R1-048.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-048.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-048.paraphrase: Monitoring is a principal QC activity; it should be performed by persons not involved in the clinical conduct of the trial at the site being monitored, the monitoring approach should be included in the monitoring plan, and the sponsor should determine the extent and nature of monitoring based on identified risks.

R1-049.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-049.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-049.paraphrase: Investigator site monitoring (including pharmacies and local laboratories as appropriate) should have its frequency determined based on identified risks, and activities and frequency should be modified using knowledge gained.
R1-049.quote: be determined based on identified risks

R1-050.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-050.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-050.paraphrase: Centralised monitoring is an evaluation of accumulated data, performed in a timely manner by the sponsor's qualified and trained persons (e.g. medical monitor, data scientist/data manager, biostatistician).
R1-050.quote: Centralised monitoring is an evaluation of accumulated data

R1-051.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-051.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-051.paraphrase: Centralised monitoring can complement and reduce site monitoring or be used on its own; centralised data analytics can help identify systemic or site-specific issues, including protocol noncompliance and potentially unreliable data.
R1-051.quote: including protocol noncompliance and potentially unreliable data

R1-052.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-052.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-052.paraphrase: Centralised monitoring may support the selection of sites and/or processes for targeted investigator site monitoring.

R1-053.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-053.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-053.paraphrase: The sponsor should develop a monitoring plan tailored to identified potential safety risks, risks to data quality and other risks to reliability of results, describing strategy, monitoring activities of all parties, methods, tools and rationale; the plan should focus on aspects that are critical to quality.
R1-053.quote: The plan should focus on aspects that are critical to quality.

R1-054.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-054.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-054.paraphrase: Monitoring of important data and processes performed outside the investigator site (e.g. those related to primary and key secondary endpoints or participant safety, such as central image reading or central laboratories) should be addressed in the monitoring plan.
R1-054.quote: should be addressed in the monitoring plan

R1-055.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-055.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-055.paraphrase: Persons performing monitoring should follow the sponsor's monitoring plan and applicable monitoring procedures.

R1-056.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-056.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-056.paraphrase: The sponsor should maintain communication with the investigator and other trial parties; each site should generally have an assigned monitor as point of contact.
R1-056.party: sponsor (gerund item); assigned monitor as site contact point

R1-057.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-057.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-057.paraphrase: Monitoring activities (per the sponsor's requirements and monitoring plan) include informing the investigator or other parties and individuals involved in the trial of relevant deviations from the protocol, GCP and applicable regulatory requirements.
R1-057.party: sponsor (monitoring activities; item phrased as gerund, no actor named)
R1-057.quote: relevant deviations from the protocol, GCP and the applicable regulatory requirements

R1-058.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-058.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-058.paraphrase: Monitoring should, if necessary, include taking appropriate action designed to prevent recurrence of the detected deviations.

R1-059.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-059.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-059.paraphrase: Important deviations should be highlighted and should be the focus of remediation efforts.
R1-059.quote: Important deviations should be highlighted and should be the focus of remediation efforts

R1-060.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-060.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-060.paraphrase: Monitoring includes informing the investigator and others of errors or omissions in source records or data acquisition tools and ensuring corrections, additions or deletions are dated, explained if necessary and their approval documented.

R1-061.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-061.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-061.paraphrase: Actions taken in relation to deviations, errors or omissions should be proportionate to their importance.
R1-061.quote: should be proportionate to their importance

R1-062.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-062.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-062.paraphrase: Monitoring includes confirming that site staff are informed about and follow the current approved protocol and other protocol-related documents.
R1-062.quote: follow the current approved protocol and other protocol-related documents

R1-063.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-063.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-063.paraphrase: Monitoring includes confirming that the investigator provides the required reports, notifications or other information in accordance with the protocol and trial procedures.
R1-063.quote: Confirming that the investigator provides the required reports, notifications or other information

R1-064.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-064.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-064.paraphrase: Monitoring of trial data includes verifying that the investigator is enrolling only eligible trial participants.
R1-064.quote: Verifying that the investigator is enrolling only eligible trial participants

R1-065.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-065.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-065.paraphrase: Monitoring of trial data (on-site and/or centralised, possibly sample-based) should identify missing data, inconsistent data, data outliers, unexpected lack of variability and protocol deviations.
R1-065.quote: Identify missing data, inconsistent data, data outliers, unexpected lack of variability and protocol deviations

R1-066.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-066.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-066.paraphrase: Monitoring of trial data should identify significant errors in data collection and reporting at a site or across sites, potential data manipulation and data integrity problems.

R1-067.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-067.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-067.paraphrase: Reports of monitoring activities should include a summary of what was reviewed, a description of significant findings, conclusions and actions required to resolve them and follow-up on their resolution including items not resolved in previous reports; content and frequency are set in sponsor procedures.
R1-067.quote: a description of significant findings, conclusions and actions required to resolve them

R1-068.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-068.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-068.paraphrase: Investigator site and centralised monitoring reports should be provided to the appropriate sponsor staff in a timely manner for review and follow-up.
R1-068.quote: in a timely manner for review and follow-up

R1-069.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-069.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-069.paraphrase: When needed, the monitoring report should describe findings requiring escalation for action and resolution.
R1-069.quote: findings requiring escalation for action and resolution

R1-070.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-070.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-070.paraphrase: The sponsor should decide on the appropriate action to be taken on escalated findings; decisions and the resolution of actions should be documented where needed.

R1-071.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-071.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-071.paraphrase: Noncompliance with the protocol, SOPs, GCP and/or applicable regulatory requirements by an investigator/institution or by member(s) of the sponsor's staff should lead to appropriate and proportionate action by the sponsor to secure compliance.
R1-071.quote: should lead to appropriate and proportionate action by the sponsor to secure compliance

R1-072.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-072.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-072.paraphrase: If noncompliance significantly affects or has the potential to significantly affect participant rights, safety or well-being or the reliability of trial results, the sponsor should perform a root cause analysis.
R1-072.quote: perform a root cause analysis, implement appropriate corrective and preventive actions

R1-073.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-073.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-073.paraphrase: For such noncompliance the sponsor should implement appropriate corrective and preventive actions and confirm their adequacy, unless otherwise justified.

R1-074.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-074.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-074.paraphrase: Serious noncompliance is described as issues likely to significantly impact the rights, safety or well-being of trial participants or the reliability of trial results.
R1-074.quote: likely to significantly impact the rights, safety or well-being

R1-075.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-075.deadline: none stated in E6(R3) (regional law sets time limits)
R1-075.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-075.paraphrase: Where the sponsor identifies serious noncompliance, it should notify the regulatory authority and/or IRB/IEC in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements, and/or the investigator, as appropriate.
R1-075.quote: (i.e., serious noncompliance), the sponsor should notify the

R1-076.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-076.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-076.paraphrase: If significant noncompliance by an investigator/institution or service provider persists despite efforts at remediation, the sponsor should consider terminating that party's participation in the trial.
R1-076.quote: should consider terminating the investigator’s/institution’s or service provider’s participation

R1-077.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-077.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-077.paraphrase: In that case the sponsor should promptly notify the regulatory authority(ies) and IRB/IEC of the serious noncompliance, as appropriate.

R1-078.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-078.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-078.paraphrase: The sponsor should also take action to minimise the impact on trial participants and on the reliability of trial results.

R1-079.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-079.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-079.paraphrase: The sponsor should take prompt action to address immediate hazards to participants, determine the causes of the hazard and take appropriate remedial actions.
R1-079.quote: take prompt action to address immediate hazards to participants

R1-080.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-080.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-080.paraphrase: The sponsor should consider whether the protocol requires amendment in response to an immediate hazard; the information on the immediate hazard, if required, and any subsequent amendment should be submitted to the IRB/IEC and/or regulatory authorities by the investigator/institution or sponsor per applicable regulatory requirements.

R1-081.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-081.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-081.paraphrase: The sponsor should apply QC to the relevant stages of data handling and focus QA and QC activities, including data review, on data of higher criticality and relevant metadata.

R1-083.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-083.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-083.paraphrase: For all computerised systems, the sponsor should ensure a process for service providers and investigator(s)/institution(s) to inform the sponsor of incidents that could potentially constitute a serious noncompliance with the protocol, trial procedures, applicable regulatory requirements or GCP (see 3.12).
R1-083.quote: a process in place for service providers and investigator(s)/institution(s)

R1-084.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-084.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-084.paraphrase: Criteria for inclusion or exclusion of trial participants from any analysis set should be pre-defined (e.g. in the protocol or statistical analysis plan), and the rationale for excluding any participant or data point clearly described and documented.
R1-084.quote: criteria for inclusion or exclusion of trial participants

R1-085.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-085.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-085.paraphrase: The sponsor (or subsequent data owner) should retain the sponsor-specific essential records in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements (see Appendix C).

R1-086.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption (EMA page lists Annex 2 Step 5 effective 15 Jan 2027); US: FDA guidance (non-binding) (FDA Annex 2 still draft)
R1-086.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-086.paraphrase: Investigator oversight should be proportionate to the importance of the data being collected and to the risks to participant rights, safety and well-being and data reliability; it may range from direct supervision to review of essential records, in person or via remote communication.
R1-086.quote: proportionate to the importance of the data being collected

R1-087.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption (EMA page lists Annex 2 Step 5 effective 15 Jan 2027); US: FDA guidance (non-binding) (FDA Annex 2 still draft)
R1-087.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-087.paraphrase: Where healthcare professionals conduct trial activities within usual clinical practice, the protocol should describe these activities and appropriate arrangements should cover information sharing, record retention, privacy and data integrity; investigator oversight should be proportionate to data criticality and ensure that resulting records meet the relevant protocol requirements.

R1-088.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption (EMA page lists Annex 2 Step 5 effective 15 Jan 2027); US: FDA guidance (non-binding) (FDA Annex 2 still draft)
R1-088.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-088.paraphrase: Sponsors considering pragmatic elements should assess whether the approach is fit for purpose and complies with applicable regulatory requirements, and ensure the protocol clearly describes how, by whom and under what circumstances these activities will be performed.

R1-089.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption (EMA page lists Annex 2 Step 5 effective 15 Jan 2027); US: FDA guidance (non-binding) (FDA Annex 2 still draft)
R1-089.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-089.paraphrase: Sponsor oversight should be proportionate to the potential impact on participant protection and reliability of results; quality control and assurance should be customised to the trial and its critical to quality factors and identified risks.
R1-089.quote: specifically customised to the clinical trial and its critical to quality factors

R1-090.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption (EMA page lists Annex 2 Step 5 effective 15 Jan 2027); US: FDA guidance (non-binding) (FDA Annex 2 still draft)
R1-090.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-090.paraphrase: Sponsors should maintain appropriate oversight of service providers, including of their essential records; where the sponsor arranges activities under investigator responsibility (e.g. home nursing), the investigator retains the ability to decide whether the proposed provider is appropriate.

R1-091.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-091.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-091.paraphrase: Critical to quality factors are attributes of a trial that are fundamental to the protection of participants, the reliability and interpretability of the trial results and the decisions made based on those results.
R1-091.quote: attributes of a trial that are fundamental to the protection of participants

R1-092.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-092.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-092.paraphrase: The investigator should ensure that the investigational product(s) are used only in accordance with the approved protocol.
R1-092.quote: used only in accordance with the approved protocol

R1-093.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-093.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-093.paraphrase: The investigator should follow the randomisation procedures, break the code only in accordance with the protocol, and promptly document and explain to the sponsor any premature unblinding (e.g. accidental, emergency, due to an SAE).
R1-093.quote: promptly document and explain to the sponsor any premature unblinding
R1-093.record: documentation and explanation of premature unblinding

R1-094.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-094.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-094.paraphrase: The investigator should be provided with timely access to data by the sponsor and is responsible for timely review of data, including relevant external data that can affect e.g. participant eligibility, treatment or safety.
R1-094.quote: be responsible for the timely review of data

R1-095.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-095.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-095.paraphrase: When using computerised systems, the investigator/institution should ensure that incidents in their use and operation which, in its judgement, may have a significant and/or persistent impact on trial data or system security are reported to the sponsor and, where applicable, to the IRB/IEC.
R1-095.quote: are reported to the sponsor and, where applicable, to the IRB/IEC

R1-096.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-096.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-096.paraphrase: The sponsor should ensure all aspects of the trial are operationally feasible and avoid unnecessary complexity, procedures and data collection; protocols, data acquisition tools and other operational documents should be fit for purpose, clear, concise and consistent.
R1-096.quote: should avoid unnecessary complexity, procedures and data collection

R1-097.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-097.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-097.paraphrase: Prior to initiating clinical trial activities, the sponsor should determine the roles and allocate trial-related activities accordingly.
R1-097.quote: the sponsor should determine the roles and allocate their trial-related activities accordingly

R1-098.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-098.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-098.paraphrase: The sponsor should obtain the investigator's/institution's and, where applicable, service provider's agreement to conduct the trial in accordance with the approved protocol and in compliance with GCP and applicable regulatory requirements.
R1-098.quote: To conduct the trial in accordance with the approved protocol

R1-099.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-099.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-099.paraphrase: The sponsor retains ultimate responsibility for transferred activities; any service provider performing trial activities should implement appropriate quality management and report to the sponsor incidents that might impact participant safety and/or trial results.
R1-099.quote: report to the sponsor incidents that might have an impact on the safety

R1-100.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-100.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-100.paraphrase: Whether the trial is completed, prematurely terminated or interim-analysed for submission, the sponsor should ensure clinical trial reports (including interim reports) are prepared and provided to regulatory authorities as required, and that reports in marketing applications meet the standards of ICH E3 or applicable requirements.
R1-100.quote: meet the standards of ICH E3

R1-102.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-102.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-102.paraphrase: Procedures for review of trial-specific data, audit trails and other relevant metadata should be in place; review should be planned, risk-based, trial-adapted and adjusted with experience.
R1-102.quote: Procedures for review of trial-specific data, audit trails and other relevant metadata

R1-104.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-104.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-104.paraphrase: Activities undertaken to finalise data sets prior to analysis should be confirmed and documented in accordance with pre-specified procedures.
R1-104.quote: should be confirmed and documented in accordance with pre-specified procedures

R1-105.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-105.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-105.paraphrase: Data finalisation activities may include reconciliation, rectification of data errors and omissions, medical coding, and compilation of and addressing the impact of noncompliance issues, including protocol deviations.
R1-105.quote: compilation of and addressing the impact of noncompliance issues, including protocol deviations

R1-106.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-106.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-106.paraphrase: Data extraction and determination of data analysis sets should take place in accordance with the planned statistical analysis and should be documented.

R1-107.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-107.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-107.paraphrase: Trial data and relevant metadata should be archived so they remain retrievable and readable and protected from unauthorised access and alteration throughout the retention period.

R1-109.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-109.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-109.paraphrase: Building adaptability into the protocol, for example acceptable ranges for specific protocol provisions, can reduce the number of deviations or the need for amendments; such adaptability should not adversely affect participant safety or scientific validity.
R1-109.quote: can reduce the number of deviations

R1-110.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-110.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-110.paraphrase: The protocol should generally include a statement that the trial will be conducted in compliance with the protocol, GCP and applicable regulatory requirements.

R1-111.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-111.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-111.paraphrase: The protocol should generally describe the selection of participants for the planned analyses, the statistical methods and procedures for handling intercurrent events and missing, unused and spurious data, aligned with target estimands where defined (see ICH E9(R1)).

R1-112.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-112.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-112.paraphrase: The protocol should generally describe identified critical to quality factors, associated risks and risk mitigation strategies, unless documented elsewhere.
R1-112.quote: Description of identified critical to quality factors, associated risks and risk mitigation strategies

R1-113.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-113.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-113.paraphrase: The protocol should generally include a summary of the monitoring approaches that are part of the quality control process.

R1-114.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-114.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-114.paraphrase: The protocol should generally include a description of the process for handling noncompliance with the protocol or GCP.
R1-114.quote: Description of the process for the handling of noncompliance with the protocol or GCP.

R1-115.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-115.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-115.paraphrase: Essential records permit evaluation of investigator and sponsor compliance with GCP and regulations and of result reliability; they are used in investigator and sponsor oversight (including monitoring), audit, inspection and IRB/IEC review; the investigator/institution should have access to, maintain and retain its essential records per applicable regulatory requirements.

R1-116.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-116.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-116.paraphrase: Essential records should be maintained in or referred to from repositories held by the sponsor and the investigator/institution, which may be referred to as trial master file (TMF) and investigator site file (ISF).
R1-116.record: trial master file; investigator site file

R1-117.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-117.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-117.paraphrase: The sponsor and investigator/institution should ensure essential records are collected and filed in a timely manner.

R1-118.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-118.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-118.paraphrase: Essential records should be retained complete, readable, readily available and directly accessible on request by regulatory authorities, monitors and auditors; alterations should be traceable.

R1-119.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-119.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-119.paraphrase: A record is essential if it is a document submitted to or issued by the regulatory authority or IRB/IEC, including related correspondence and documentation of regulatory decisions or approvals/favourable opinions.
R1-119.record: regulatory and IRB/IEC submissions and correspondence

R1-120.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-120.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-120.paraphrase: A record is essential if it documents sponsor oversight of site selection, monitoring and audit and provides information on arising issues/noncompliance and deviations detected and implementation of corrective and preventative actions.
R1-120.quote: arising issues/noncompliance and deviations detected and implementation of corrective and preventative actions
R1-120.record: oversight records on deviations and CAPA

R1-121.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-121.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-121.paraphrase: A record is essential if it documents compliance with the protocol and/or procedures for data management, statistical analysis and production of interim and final reports.

R1-122.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-122.deadline: retention period per applicable regulatory requirements
R1-122.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-122.paraphrase: Trial records listed in the Essential Records Table should be retained when produced; the table is not exhaustive, and some records depend on trial design, conduct and risk-proportionate management (C.3.3); no fixed retention period is given (retention per applicable regulatory requirements).

R1-123.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-123.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-123.paraphrase: Essential Records Table row: 'Records and reports of noncompliance including protocol deviations and corrective and preventative actions' - essential and to be retained if produced (not marked as required before trial start).
R1-123.quote: Records and reports of noncompliance including protocol deviations and corrective and preventative actions
R1-123.record: deviation and noncompliance records and reports; CAPA records

R1-124.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-124.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-124.paraphrase: Essential Records Table rows: 'Site monitoring reports (including site selection, initiation, routine and close-out)' and 'Centralised monitoring reports' - essential and to be retained if produced.
R1-124.record: site monitoring reports; centralised monitoring reports

R1-125.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-125.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-125.paraphrase: Essential Records Table row: 'Documentation relating to data finalisation for analysis' (e.g. query resolutions, SAE reconciliation, QC reports, coding completion, output data sets) - essential and to be retained if produced.

R1-126.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-126.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-126.paraphrase: Essential Records Table row: 'Documentation relating to the statistical considerations and analysis' including analysis sets decisions - essential and to be retained if produced.
R1-126.record: analysis sets decisions; analysis data sets

R1-127.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-127.deadline: generally before the start of the trial (asterisked records)
R1-127.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-127.paraphrase: Essential Records Table row: 'Trial-specific plans (e.g., risk management, monitoring, safety, data management, data validation and statistical analysis) and procedures'; the risk management, monitoring, safety, data management and data validation plans are asterisked, i.e. should generally be in place before trial start (C.2.5); the statistical analysis plan is not asterisked.

R1-128.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-128.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-128.paraphrase: Essential Records Table rows: 'Signed protocol and subsequent amendments during the trial' and 'Regulatory authority(ies) authorisation, approval and/or notification of the protocol and of subsequent amendments (where required)' - essential and to be retained.

R1-129.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-129.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-129.paraphrase: Essential Records Table row: 'Interim (where applicable) and final clinical trial reports' - essential and to be retained.

R1-133.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-133.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-133.paraphrase: Monitoring is the act of overseeing the progress of a clinical trial and ensuring it is conducted, recorded and reported per the protocol, SOPs, GCP and applicable regulatory requirements.

R1-134.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-134.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-134.paraphrase: A monitoring plan is a document that describes the strategy, methods, responsibilities and requirements for monitoring the trial.

R1-135.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-135.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-135.paraphrase: A monitoring report is a documented report following site and/or centralised monitoring activities.
R1-135.quote: A documented report following site and/or centralised monitoring activities.

R1-136.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-136.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-136.paraphrase: Essential records are the documents and data (and relevant metadata), in any format, that facilitate trial management and allow evaluation of methods used, factors affecting the trial and actions taken, to determine reliability of results and verify conduct per GCP and regulations (see Appendix C).

R1-140.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-140.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-140.paraphrase: The sponsor is an individual, company, institution or organisation that takes responsibility for initiation, management and arrangement of financing of a trial; with several sponsors, unattributed responsibilities lie with all.

R1-141.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-141.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-141.paraphrase: The investigator is the person responsible for the conduct of the trial at a site, including the participants under their responsibility; 'investigator/institution' expectations may apply to the investigator and/or institution.

R1-142.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-142.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-142.paraphrase: An IRB/IEC is an independent body of medical and non-medical members responsible for protecting participants' rights, safety and well-being, inter alia by reviewing and approving/providing favourable opinion on the protocol.

R1-143.binding_route: EU: via EU CTR Art. 47 / EMA adoption; US: FDA guidance (non-binding)
R1-143.doc: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Final version, Step 4, consolidated with Annex 2, 16 June 2026
R1-143.paraphrase: Regulatory authorities are bodies having the power to regulate, including those reviewing protocols and clinical data and conducting inspections; sometimes called competent authorities.

R2-001.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-001.doc: ICH E8(R1) General Considerations for Clinical Studies, Final version, Step 4, adopted 6 October 2021
R2-001.paraphrase: Quality by design means concentrating on critical to quality factors so that participants' rights, safety and well-being are protected, results are reliable and meaningful, and risks to those factors are managed in proportion to the risk. A framework for identifying and reviewing these factors supports the approach from design and planning through conduct, analysis and reporting.

R2-002.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-002.doc: ICH E8(R1) General Considerations for Clinical Studies, Final version, Step 4, adopted 6 October 2021
R2-002.paraphrase: Quality is built in prospectively through attention to the protocol, procedures, operational plans and training, which can raise the chance of answering the study questions and avoiding important errors. Retrospective document and data review, monitoring and audits are an important part of quality assurance but, even combined, are not sufficient on their own to ensure study quality (statement, no 'should').

R2-003.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-003.doc: ICH E8(R1) General Considerations for Clinical Studies, Final version, Step 4, adopted 6 October 2021
R2-003.paraphrase: Critical to quality factors are attributes of a study whose integrity is fundamental to protecting participants, to the reliability and interpretability of the results, and to the decisions based on them. They are critical because errors in design or conduct that undermine them would also undermine the reliability or ethics of those decisions.
R2-003.quote: attributes of a study whose integrity is fundamental

R2-004.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-004.doc: ICH E8(R1) General Considerations for Clinical Studies, Final version, Step 4, adopted 6 October 2021
R2-004.paraphrase: The sponsor and the other parties designing quality into a study should identify its critical to quality factors; each study should have a basic set of quality-relevant factors identified, with emphasis on those that are critical to study quality.
R2-004.party: The sponsor and other parties designing quality into a clinical study

R2-005.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-005.doc: ICH E8(R1) General Considerations for Clinical Studies, Final version, Step 4, adopted 6 October 2021
R2-005.paraphrase: Critical to quality factors should be considered as a whole so that interdependencies between them are recognised.

R2-006.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-006.doc: ICH E8(R1) General Considerations for Clinical Studies, Final version, Step 4, adopted 6 October 2021
R2-006.paraphrase: Study design should reflect current knowledge of the drug, the condition, the underlying biology and the intended population; knowledge accumulated at each development stage continues to inform which factors are critical and which controls are used to manage them.
verify_raw: [verify] sentence content from a single fetch (F02)

R2-007.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-007.doc: ICH E8(R1) General Considerations for Clinical Studies, Final version, Step 4, adopted 6 October 2021
R2-007.paraphrase: Once critical to quality factors are identified, the risks to them are to be determined and a decision taken whether each risk is acceptable or should be mitigated, based on its probability, detectability and impact (framed in the source as important).
R2-007.party: The sponsor and other parties designing quality into a clinical study

R2-008.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-008.doc: ICH E8(R1) General Considerations for Clinical Studies, Final version, Step 4, adopted 6 October 2021
R2-008.paraphrase: The term risk is used in the sense of general risk management methodology and applies to all factors of a study.
verify_raw: [verify] sentence content from a single fetch (F02)

R2-009.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-009.doc: ICH E8(R1) General Considerations for Clinical Studies, Final version, Step 4, adopted 6 October 2021
R2-009.paraphrase: Where a risk to a critical to quality factor is to be mitigated, the necessary control processes should be put in place and communicated, and the necessary mitigating actions taken.
R2-009.party: The sponsor and other parties designing quality into a clinical study

R2-010.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-010.doc: ICH E8(R1) General Considerations for Clinical Studies, Final version, Step 4, adopted 6 October 2021
R2-010.paraphrase: Proactive, ongoing communication about critical to quality factors and risk mitigation activities supports a shared understanding by sponsor and sites of priorities and resource allocation (presented as beneficial, no 'should').
verify_raw: [verify] sentence content from a single fetch (F02)

R2-011.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-011.doc: ICH E8(R1) General Considerations for Clinical Studies, Final version, Step 4, adopted 6 October 2021
R2-011.paraphrase: Proactive support, for example site training appropriate to role and a description in the protocol of the critical to quality factors and potential mitigation measures, helps ensure the protocol, procedures and associated plans are implemented correctly.

R2-012.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-012.doc: ICH E8(R1) General Considerations for Clinical Studies, Final version, Step 4, adopted 6 October 2021
R2-012.paraphrase: Because perfection in every aspect is rarely achievable, or only with disproportionate resources, quality factors should be prioritised at the design stage to identify those that are critical, and procedures should be proportionate to the risks and to the importance of the information collected.

R2-013.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-013.doc: ICH E8(R1) General Considerations for Clinical Studies, Final version, Step 4, adopted 6 October 2021
R2-013.paraphrase: Critical to quality factors should be clear and should not be cluttered with minor issues, for example those arising from extensive secondary objectives or from processes and data collection unrelated to participant protection or the primary objectives.

R2-014.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-014.doc: ICH E8(R1) General Considerations for Clinical Studies, Final version, Step 4, adopted 6 October 2021
R2-014.paraphrase: Identifying critical to quality factors should include judging whether the objectives can be met effectively and efficiently with the chosen design and data sources; the quality approach asks whether objectives are clear, the design answers the question, the question matters to patients and hypotheses are specific and valid. Early patient consultation can support this.

R2-015.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-015.doc: ICH E8(R1) General Considerations for Clinical Studies, Final version, Step 4, adopted 6 October 2021
R2-015.paraphrase: Study designs should be operationally feasible and avoid unnecessary complexity; protocols and data collection tools should allow the study to be conducted as designed and avoid unnecessary data collection.

R2-016.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-016.doc: ICH E8(R1) General Considerations for Clinical Studies, Final version, Step 4, adopted 6 October 2021
