R2-085.doc: ICH Harmonised Tripartite Guideline E9 Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials, Current Step 4 version, 5 February 1998
R2-085.paraphrase: Because some problems cannot be foreseen, the handling of irregularities may sometimes be deferred to the blind review at the end of the trial, if the protocol so specifies.
verify_raw: [verify] sentence content from a single fetch (F19)

R2-086.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-086.doc: ICH Harmonised Tripartite Guideline E9 Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials, Current Step 4 version, 5 February 1998
R2-086.paraphrase: The per protocol set is the subset of the full analysis set that is more compliant with the protocol, characterised by a pre-specified minimal exposure to treatment, availability of primary variable measurements, and absence of major protocol violations, including violation of entry criteria.
R2-086.quote: the absence of any major protocol violations including the violation of entry criteria
verify_raw: [verify] printed page: 23 per F19, 24 per F21

R2-087.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-087.doc: ICH Harmonised Tripartite Guideline E9 Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials, Current Step 4 version, 5 February 1998
R2-087.paraphrase: The precise reasons for excluding subjects from the per protocol set should be fully defined and documented before the blind is broken.
verify_raw: [verify] printed page: 23 per F19, 24 per F21

R2-088.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-088.doc: ICH Harmonised Tripartite Guideline E9 Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials, Current Step 4 version, 5 February 1998
R2-088.paraphrase: Protocol violations other than those used to define the per protocol set should be fully identified and summarised; relevant violations may include errors in treatment assignment, use of excluded medication, poor compliance, loss to follow-up and missing data.

R2-089.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-089.doc: ICH Harmonised Tripartite Guideline E9 Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials, Current Step 4 version, 5 February 1998
R2-089.paraphrase: It is good practice to assess the pattern of such problems across treatment groups with respect to frequency and time of occurrence.
verify_raw: [verify] sentence content from a single fetch (F20)

R2-090.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-090.doc: ICH Harmonised Tripartite Guideline E9 Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials, Current Step 4 version, 5 February 1998
R2-090.paraphrase: It is generally advantageous to show that the main results are not sensitive to the choice of analysed subjects; in confirmatory trials it is usually appropriate to plan analyses of both the full analysis set and the per protocol set so that differences can be discussed, and exclusion of a substantial proportion of subjects from the per protocol set casts some doubt on the overall validity of the trial.
verify_raw: [verify] section content from a single fetch (F20); start page 24 per TOC and F22, 25 per F20

R2-091.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-091.doc: ICH Harmonised Tripartite Guideline E9 Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials, Current Step 4 version, 5 February 1998
R2-091.paraphrase: Decisions taken during the blinded pre-analysis review, such as excluding subjects or data from the analysis sets, should be described in the report and distinguished from decisions taken after unblinding.

R2-092.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-092.doc: ICH Harmonised Tripartite Guideline E9 Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials, Current Step 4 version, 5 February 1998
R2-092.paraphrase: All reasons for exclusion from analysis should be documented, including, for subjects in the full analysis set but not the per protocol set, the reasons for their exclusion from the latter.

R2-093.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-093.doc: ICH Harmonised Tripartite Guideline E9 Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials, Current Step 4 version, 5 February 1998
R2-093.paraphrase: The effect on the main analyses of all losses of subjects or data, withdrawals from treatment and major protocol violations should be considered carefully.

R2-094.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-094.doc: ICH Harmonised Tripartite Guideline E9 Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials, Current Step 4 version, 5 February 1998
R2-094.paraphrase: Subjects lost to follow-up, withdrawn from treatment or with a severe protocol violation should be identified and described, including their reasons and the relationship to treatment and outcome.

R2-095.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-095.doc: ICH Harmonised Tripartite Guideline E9 Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials, Current Step 4 version, 5 February 1998
R2-095.paraphrase: When summarising the clinical database across trials, the handling of protocol violators and deviators, together with the other conventions listed, should be kept compatible unless there are valid reasons not to.

R2-096.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-096.deadline: between trial completion and breaking of the blind
R2-096.doc: ICH Harmonised Tripartite Guideline E9 Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials, Current Step 4 version, 5 February 1998
R2-096.paraphrase: Blind review is the checking and assessment of data between trial completion and the breaking of the blind, in order to finalise the planned analysis.
verify_raw: [verify] glossary wording from a single fetch (F20)

R2-097.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-097.doc: ICH E9(R1) Addendum on Estimands and Sensitivity Analysis in Clinical Trials to the Guideline on Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials, Final version, Step 4, adopted 20 November 2019
R2-097.paraphrase: The addendum revisits per protocol analysis, asking whether the need to explore the impact of protocol violations and deviations can be met in a way that is less biased and more interpretable than a naive per protocol analysis.

R2-098.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-098.doc: ICH E9(R1) Addendum on Estimands and Sensitivity Analysis in Clinical Trials to the Guideline on Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials, Final version, Step 4, adopted 20 November 2019
R2-098.paraphrase: Discontinuation of randomised treatment is distinguished from withdrawal from the study: treatment discontinuation is an intercurrent event to be addressed in the estimand, whereas study withdrawal leads to missing data.
verify_raw: [verify] sentence content from a single fetch (F23)

R2-099.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-099.doc: ICH E9(R1) Addendum on Estimands and Sensitivity Analysis in Clinical Trials to the Guideline on Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials, Final version, Step 4, adopted 20 November 2019
R2-099.paraphrase: Very granular events, such as a single missed dose of a chronic treatment or a dose taken at the wrong time of day, need not be handled as intercurrent events if they are not expected to affect interpretation of the variable.
verify_raw: [verify] sentence content from a single fetch (F23)

R2-100.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-100.doc: ICH E9(R1) Addendum on Estimands and Sensitivity Analysis in Clinical Trials to the Guideline on Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials, Final version, Step 4, adopted 20 November 2019
R2-100.paraphrase: Where the relevance of an intercurrent event depends on its reason, magnitude or timing, that additional information should be defined and recorded accurately in the trial.
R2-100.record: trial data on reason, magnitude and timing of the event

R2-101.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-101.doc: ICH E9(R1) Addendum on Estimands and Sensitivity Analysis in Clinical Trials to the Guideline on Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials, Final version, Step 4, adopted 20 November 2019
R2-101.paraphrase: Withdrawal from the trial and other reasons for missing data, such as administrative censoring, are not intercurrent events in themselves, although a subject may have experienced an intercurrent event before withdrawing.
verify_raw: [verify] sentence content from a single fetch (F23)

R2-102.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-102.doc: ICH E9(R1) Addendum on Estimands and Sensitivity Analysis in Clinical Trials to the Guideline on Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials, Final version, Step 4, adopted 20 November 2019
R2-102.paraphrase: For non-inferiority and equivalence trials, which are not conservative, minimising the number of protocol violations and deviations, non-adherence and withdrawals is important.

R2-103.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-103.doc: ICH E9(R1) Addendum on Estimands and Sensitivity Analysis in Clinical Trials to the Guideline on Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials, Final version, Step 4, adopted 20 November 2019
R2-103.paraphrase: Efforts should be made to collect all data relevant to support estimation; discontinuation, switching or added medication does not mean the variable cannot be measured afterwards.
verify_raw: [verify] exact sentence boundaries; confirmed only as short phrases (F24)

R2-104.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-104.doc: ICH E9(R1) Addendum on Estimands and Sensitivity Analysis in Clinical Trials to the Guideline on Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials, Final version, Step 4, adopted 20 November 2019
R2-104.paraphrase: A prospective plan to collect informative reasons why intended data are missing may help distinguish intercurrent events from missing data, for example by recording a loss to follow-up more accurately as discontinuation due to lack of efficacy.

R2-105.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-105.doc: ICH E9(R1) Addendum on Estimands and Sensitivity Analysis in Clinical Trials to the Guideline on Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials, Final version, Step 4, adopted 20 November 2019
R2-105.paraphrase: Measures can be implemented to retain subjects in the trial.

R2-106.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-106.doc: ICH E9(R1) Addendum on Estimands and Sensitivity Analysis in Clinical Trials to the Guideline on Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials, Final version, Step 4, adopted 20 November 2019
R2-106.paraphrase: The addendum contrasts protocol violations and deviations with intercurrent events: a violation or deviation such as an out-of-window visit might exclude a subject from the per protocol set without any intercurrent event, and a subject could experience an intercurrent event such as death without having deviated from the protocol. It does not state this as a formal rule.

R2-107.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-107.doc: ICH E9(R1) Addendum on Estimands and Sensitivity Analysis in Clinical Trials to the Guideline on Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials, Final version, Step 4, adopted 20 November 2019
R2-107.paraphrase: Despite these differences, events that affect the interpretation or existence of measurements are addressed in the estimand description; an estimand with an aligned analysis method might better address the objective usually given to per protocol analysis, in which case per protocol analysis may add little further insight.
R2-107.quote: Notwithstanding the differences between violations and deviations from the protocol and intercurrent events

R2-108.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-108.doc: ICH E9(R1) Addendum on Estimands and Sensitivity Analysis in Clinical Trials to the Guideline on Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials, Final version, Step 4, adopted 20 November 2019
R2-108.paraphrase: Summaries of the number and timing of each intercurrent event in each treatment group should be reported in the clinical trial report (term used in the source).

R2-109.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline; EU route owned by R3, US route owned by R4
R2-109.doc: ICH E9(R1) Addendum on Estimands and Sensitivity Analysis in Clinical Trials to the Guideline on Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials, Final version, Step 4, adopted 20 November 2019
R2-109.paraphrase: Where intercurrent events not foreseen at the design stage are identified during trial conduct, the report should discuss the analysis choices made and their effect on the estimand, on the treatment effect estimated and on interpretation of the results.

R2-111.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline adopted 19 November 2025; regional implementation not checked (R3, R4)
R2-111.doc: ICH Harmonised Guideline M11 Structure and Content of Clinical Protocols - Clinical Electronic Structured Harmonised Protocol (CeSHarP), Final version, Step 4, adopted 19 November 2025
R2-111.paraphrase: The M11 Template gives a uniform table of contents and common headers for any medicinal product trial; top-level headings are fixed while lower-level sections may be adapted; the Template should be used together with the other ICH guidelines relevant to the conduct of clinical trials.
verify_raw: [verify] section content from a single fetch (F30); Step 4 status confirmed in F26

R2-112.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline adopted 19 November 2025; regional implementation not checked (R3, R4)
R2-112.doc: ICH M11 Template - Clinical Electronic Structured Harmonised Protocol (CeSHarP), Final version, Step 4, adopted 19 November 2025
R2-112.paraphrase: Template conventions: instructional text is removed before the protocol is finalised; level 1 and level 2 headings are required, must not be deleted or modified, and are kept with 'Not applicable' where they do not apply; optional lower-level headings may be omitted and additional headings added.
verify_raw: [verify] section label of the conventions part and wording; single fetch (F31)

R2-113.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline adopted 19 November 2025; regional implementation not checked (R3, R4)
R2-113.doc: ICH M11 Template - Clinical Electronic Structured Harmonised Protocol (CeSHarP), Final version, Step 4, adopted 19 November 2025
R2-113.paraphrase: Prospective approval of protocol deviations from recruitment and enrolment criteria, known as protocol waivers or exemptions, is not permitted.
verify_raw: [verify] whether the sentence is fixed universal text or instructional text of the template

R2-114.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline adopted 19 November 2025; regional implementation not checked (R3, R4)
R2-114.doc: ICH M11 Template - Clinical Electronic Structured Harmonised Protocol (CeSHarP), Final version, Step 4, adopted 19 November 2025
R2-114.paraphrase: The protocol describes how adherence to the trial intervention will be monitored and documented (for example accountability records, diaries, concentration measurements), lists the mandatory adherence records and identifies which records are source records (imperative template instruction).

R2-115.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline adopted 19 November 2025; regional implementation not checked (R3, R4)
R2-115.doc: ICH M11 Template - Clinical Electronic Structured Harmonised Protocol (CeSHarP), Final version, Step 4, adopted 19 November 2025
R2-115.paraphrase: The protocol describes the trial-level analysis sets, aligned with the estimands, and specifies the analysis set used for each analysis; the instruction does not mention protocol deviations (imperative template instruction).
verify_raw: [verify] instruction text from a single fetch (F29); heading listed in F28

R2-116.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline adopted 19 November 2025; regional implementation not checked (R3, R4)
R2-116.doc: ICH M11 Template - Clinical Electronic Structured Harmonised Protocol (CeSHarP), Final version, Step 4, adopted 19 November 2025
R2-116.paraphrase: Under the heading Risk-Based Quality Management, the protocol describes the identified critical to quality factors, the associated risks and the risk mitigation strategies for the trial, or refers to the location where this information is described and updated during the trial based on emerging data (imperative template instruction).
R2-116.quote: Describe the identified critical to quality factors, associated risks and risk mitigation strategies

R2-117.binding_route: ICH Step 4 guideline adopted 19 November 2025; regional implementation not checked (R3, R4)
R2-117.doc: ICH M11 Template - Clinical Electronic Structured Harmonised Protocol (CeSHarP), Final version, Step 4, adopted 19 November 2025
R2-117.paraphrase: Under the heading Protocol Deviations, the protocol describes the plans for detecting, reviewing and reporting any deviations from the protocol, or refers to a separate document; the template gives no definition of important deviations (imperative template instruction).
R2-117.quote: Describe plans for detecting, reviewing, and reporting any deviations from the protocol

R3-001.doc: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 on clinical trials on medicinal products for human use, OJ L 158, 27.5.2014 (page reference); wording read in EUR-Lex consolidated text 02014R0536-20221205 (05.12.2022)
R3-001.paraphrase: Defines the ethics committee as an independent body established in a Member State that is empowered to give opinions under the Regulation, taking the views of laypersons into account.

R3-002.doc: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 on clinical trials on medicinal products for human use, OJ L 158, 27.5.2014 (page reference); wording read in EUR-Lex consolidated text 02014R0536-20221205 (05.12.2022)
R3-002.paraphrase: Defines the Member State concerned as the Member State where an application for authorisation of a clinical trial or of a substantial modification was submitted under Chapter II or III. It is the recipient of the serious breach, unexpected event and urgent safety measure notifications.

R3-004.doc: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 on clinical trials on medicinal products for human use, OJ L 158, 27.5.2014 (page reference); wording read in EUR-Lex consolidated text 02014R0536-20221205 (05.12.2022)
R3-004.paraphrase: Defines the sponsor as the individual, company, institution or organisation that takes responsibility for initiating and managing the trial and for setting up its financing.
R3-004.quote: takes responsibility for the initiation, for the management

R3-005.doc: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 on clinical trials on medicinal products for human use, OJ L 158, 27.5.2014 (page reference); wording read in EUR-Lex consolidated text 02014R0536-20221205 (05.12.2022)
R3-005.paraphrase: Defines the investigator as the individual responsible for the conduct of a clinical trial at a clinical trial site.
R3-005.quote: an individual responsible for the conduct of a clinical trial

R3-008.doc: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 on clinical trials on medicinal products for human use, OJ L 158, 27.5.2014 (page reference); wording read in EUR-Lex consolidated text 02014R0536-20221205 (05.12.2022)
R3-008.paraphrase: Defines the end of a clinical trial as the last visit of the last subject, or a later point defined in the protocol. This event starts the 25-year archiving period of Art. 58.

R3-012.deadline: within 30 days after the day the marketing authorisation has been granted (or procedure completed / application withdrawn)
R3-012.doc: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 on clinical trials on medicinal products for human use, OJ L 158, 27.5.2014 (page reference); wording read in EUR-Lex consolidated text 02014R0536-20221205 (05.12.2022)
R3-012.paraphrase: Fourth subparagraph of Art. 37(4): where the trial was intended to be used for obtaining a marketing authorisation, the applicant for marketing authorisation submits the CSR to the EU database within 30 days after the authorisation is granted, the procedure is completed or the application is withdrawn. Process-end boundary for CSR reporting of deviations.

R3-013.deadline: without undue delay but not later than in 15 days of the date of the temporary halt or early termination
R3-013.doc: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 on clinical trials on medicinal products for human use, OJ L 158, 27.5.2014 (page reference); wording read in EUR-Lex consolidated text 02014R0536-20221205 (05.12.2022)
R3-013.paraphrase: Art. 38 covers temporary halt or early termination by the sponsor for reasons of subject safety, not urgent safety measures. A halt or early termination for reasons of a change of the benefit-risk balance must be notified to the Member States concerned through the EU portal without undue delay but not later than 15 days of the date of the halt or termination, with the reasons and the follow-up measures (passive wording; the sponsor per the title).
R3-013.party: not named in Art. 38(1) (passive voice); article title: 'by the sponsor'
R3-013.record: temporary halt / early termination notification in CTIS

R3-016.doc: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 on clinical trials on medicinal products for human use, OJ L 158, 27.5.2014 (page reference); wording read in EUR-Lex consolidated text 02014R0536-20221205 (05.12.2022)
R3-016.paraphrase: First (unnumbered) paragraph: the sponsor must ensure the trial is conducted in accordance with the protocol and with the principles of good clinical practice. This is the EU legal basis for protocol compliance and for acting on deviations.
R3-016.party: The sponsor of a clinical trial
R3-016.quote: in accordance with the protocol and with the principles of good clinical practice

R3-017.doc: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 on clinical trials on medicinal products for human use, OJ L 158, 27.5.2014 (page reference); wording read in EUR-Lex consolidated text 02014R0536-20221205 (05.12.2022)
R3-017.paraphrase: First (unnumbered) paragraph: the investigator, jointly with the sponsor, must ensure the trial is conducted in accordance with the protocol and the principles of good clinical practice.
R3-017.quote: in accordance with the protocol and with the principles of good clinical practice

R3-018.binding_route: EU: directly applicable regulation; ICH GCP is not itself law but must be taken into appropriate account (Art. 47 second paragraph)
R3-018.doc: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 on clinical trials on medicinal products for human use, OJ L 158, 27.5.2014 (page reference); wording read in EUR-Lex consolidated text 02014R0536-20221205 (05.12.2022)
R3-018.paraphrase: Second (unnumbered) paragraph: when drawing up the protocol and applying the Regulation and the protocol, the sponsor must also take appropriate account of quality standards and the ICH GCP guidelines, without prejudice to other Union law or Commission guidelines. This is the EU legal hook for ICH E6(R3).
R3-018.quote: shall also take appropriate account of the quality standards and the ICH guidelines

R3-019.binding_route: EU: directly applicable regulation; ICH GCP is not itself law but must be taken into appropriate account (Art. 47 second paragraph)
R3-019.doc: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 on clinical trials on medicinal products for human use, OJ L 158, 27.5.2014 (page reference); wording read in EUR-Lex consolidated text 02014R0536-20221205 (05.12.2022)
R3-019.paraphrase: Second (unnumbered) paragraph: the investigator, when applying the Regulation and the protocol, must likewise take appropriate account of quality standards and the ICH GCP guidelines.
R3-019.quote: shall also take appropriate account of the quality standards and the ICH guidelines

R3-020.doc: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 on clinical trials on medicinal products for human use, OJ L 158, 27.5.2014 (page reference); wording read in EUR-Lex consolidated text 02014R0536-20221205 (05.12.2022)
R3-020.paraphrase: Third (unnumbered) paragraph: the Commission must make publicly available the detailed ICH GCP guidelines referred to in the second paragraph.

R3-021.doc: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 on clinical trials on medicinal products for human use, OJ L 158, 27.5.2014 (page reference); wording read in EUR-Lex consolidated text 02014R0536-20221205 (05.12.2022)
R3-021.paraphrase: The sponsor must adequately monitor trial conduct to verify that subject rights, safety and well-being are protected, that reported data are reliable and robust, and that conduct complies with the Regulation. Monitoring is the legal basis for identifying deviations at sites.
R3-021.quote: shall adequately monitor the conduct of a clinical trial

R3-022.doc: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 on clinical trials on medicinal products for human use, OJ L 158, 27.5.2014 (page reference); wording read in EUR-Lex consolidated text 02014R0536-20221205 (05.12.2022)
R3-022.paraphrase: The sponsor determines the extent and nature of monitoring on the basis of an assessment of all trial characteristics, including whether it is a low-intervention trial, its objective and methodology, and the degree to which the intervention deviates from normal clinical practice. Risk-proportionate monitoring basis.

R3-023.deadline: without undue delay but not later than seven days of becoming aware of that breach
R3-023.doc: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 on clinical trials on medicinal products for human use, OJ L 158, 27.5.2014 (page reference); wording read in EUR-Lex consolidated text 02014R0536-20221205 (05.12.2022)
R3-023.paraphrase: The sponsor must notify the Member States concerned, through the EU portal, of a serious breach of the Regulation or of the protocol version applicable at the time of the breach, without undue delay and at the latest seven days after becoming aware of it. The clock starts at sponsor awareness.
R3-023.quote: the version of the protocol applicable at the time of the breach

R3-024.doc: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 on clinical trials on medicinal products for human use, OJ L 158, 27.5.2014 (page reference); wording read in EUR-Lex consolidated text 02014R0536-20221205 (05.12.2022)
R3-024.paraphrase: For Art. 52, a serious breach is a breach likely to affect to a significant degree the safety and rights of a subject or the reliability and robustness of the data generated in the trial. Art. 2 contains no definition of serious breach; this is the only legal definition.
R3-024.quote: likely to affect to a significant degree the safety and rights of a subject

R3-025.deadline: without undue delay but no later than 15 days from the date the sponsor became aware of this event
R3-025.doc: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 on clinical trials on medicinal products for human use, OJ L 158, 27.5.2014 (page reference); wording read in EUR-Lex consolidated text 02014R0536-20221205 (05.12.2022)
R3-025.paraphrase: The sponsor must notify the Member States concerned, through the EU portal, of unexpected events that affect the benefit-risk balance but are not suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions under Art. 42, without undue delay but no later than 15 days from the date the sponsor became aware of the event.

R3-027.doc: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 on clinical trials on medicinal products for human use, OJ L 158, 27.5.2014 (page reference); wording read in EUR-Lex consolidated text 02014R0536-20221205 (05.12.2022)
R3-027.paraphrase: Where an unexpected event is likely to seriously affect the benefit-risk balance, the sponsor must take appropriate urgent safety measures to protect the subjects. Art. 54 (not Art. 38) is the urgent safety measure article.
R3-027.quote: Where an unexpected event is likely to seriously affect the benefit-risk balance

R3-028.doc: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 on clinical trials on medicinal products for human use, OJ L 158, 27.5.2014 (page reference); wording read in EUR-Lex consolidated text 02014R0536-20221205 (05.12.2022)
R3-028.paraphrase: The investigator is also obliged to take appropriate urgent safety measures to protect subjects where an unexpected event is likely to seriously affect the benefit-risk balance.
R3-028.quote: Where an unexpected event is likely to seriously affect the benefit-risk balance

R3-029.deadline: without undue delay but no later than seven days from the date the measures have been taken
R3-029.doc: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 on clinical trials on medicinal products for human use, OJ L 158, 27.5.2014 (page reference); wording read in EUR-Lex consolidated text 02014R0536-20221205 (05.12.2022)
R3-029.paraphrase: The sponsor must notify the Member States concerned, through the EU portal, of the event and the measures taken. The seven-day clock runs from the date the measures were taken, not from awareness.
R3-029.quote: no later than seven days from the date the measures have been taken
R3-029.record: urgent safety measure notification in CTIS

R3-030.doc: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 on clinical trials on medicinal products for human use, OJ L 158, 27.5.2014 (page reference); wording read in EUR-Lex consolidated text 02014R0536-20221205 (05.12.2022)
R3-030.paraphrase: Art. 54 applies without prejudice to Chapter III (authorisation procedure for a substantial modification) and Chapter VII (safety reporting), so urgent safety measures do not replace those obligations. EUCTR-QA Q&A 7.27 expects a USM that requires a protocol update to be followed by a substantial modification submission (R3-103).
R3-030.quote: This Article is without prejudice to Chapters III and VII.

R3-031.doc: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 on clinical trials on medicinal products for human use, OJ L 158, 27.5.2014 (page reference); wording read in EUR-Lex consolidated text 02014R0536-20221205 (05.12.2022)
R3-031.paraphrase: The sponsor or investigator, as applicable, must record, process, handle and store all clinical trial information so that it can be accurately reported, interpreted and verified, while protecting subject confidentiality and personal data. Basis for documenting deviations.
R3-031.party: the sponsor or the investigator, as applicable

R3-032.doc: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 on clinical trials on medicinal products for human use, OJ L 158, 27.5.2014 (page reference); wording read in EUR-Lex consolidated text 02014R0536-20221205 (05.12.2022)
R3-032.paraphrase: First (unnumbered) paragraph: the sponsor must keep a clinical trial master file that at all times contains the essential documents allowing verification of trial conduct and data quality, readily available and directly accessible to the Member States on request.
R3-032.quote: readily available, and directly accessible upon request, to the Member States

R3-033.doc: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 on clinical trials on medicinal products for human use, OJ L 158, 27.5.2014 (page reference); wording read in EUR-Lex consolidated text 02014R0536-20221205 (05.12.2022)
R3-033.paraphrase: First (unnumbered) paragraph: the investigator must also keep a clinical trial master file with the essential documents, readily available and directly accessible to the Member States on request.
R3-033.quote: readily available, and directly accessible upon request, to the Member States

R3-034.doc: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 on clinical trials on medicinal products for human use, OJ L 158, 27.5.2014 (page reference); wording read in EUR-Lex consolidated text 02014R0536-20221205 (05.12.2022)
R3-034.paraphrase: Second (unnumbered) paragraph: the sponsor and investigator master files may differ in content where justified by the different nature of their responsibilities.

R3-035.deadline: retain at least 25 years after the end of the clinical trial
R3-035.doc: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 on clinical trials on medicinal products for human use, OJ L 158, 27.5.2014 (page reference); wording read in EUR-Lex consolidated text 02014R0536-20221205 (05.12.2022)
R3-035.paraphrase: First (unnumbered) paragraph: unless other Union law requires longer, the sponsor must archive the content of the master file for at least 25 years after the end of the trial; subjects' medical files are archived under national law.
R3-035.quote: for at least 25 years after the end of the clinical trial

R3-036.deadline: retain at least 25 years after the end of the clinical trial
R3-036.doc: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 on clinical trials on medicinal products for human use, OJ L 158, 27.5.2014 (page reference); wording read in EUR-Lex consolidated text 02014R0536-20221205 (05.12.2022)
R3-036.paraphrase: First (unnumbered) paragraph: the investigator must likewise archive the content of the master file for at least 25 years after the end of the trial, with medical files under national law.
R3-036.quote: for at least 25 years after the end of the clinical trial

R3-037.doc: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 on clinical trials on medicinal products for human use, OJ L 158, 27.5.2014 (page reference); wording read in EUR-Lex consolidated text 02014R0536-20221205 (05.12.2022)
R3-037.paraphrase: Second (unnumbered) paragraph: the content of the master file must be archived so that it is readily available and accessible, upon request, to the competent authorities; the fifth paragraph requires archiving media that keep the content complete and legible for the whole period.
R3-037.party: not named (passive voice); archiving duty sits with the sponsor and the investigator (first paragraph)

R3-038.doc: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 on clinical trials on medicinal products for human use, OJ L 158, 27.5.2014 (page reference); wording read in EUR-Lex consolidated text 02014R0536-20221205 (05.12.2022)
R3-038.paraphrase: Fourth (unnumbered) paragraph: the sponsor must appoint individuals within its organisation responsible for archives, and access to archives is restricted to those individuals.
R3-038.quote: The sponsor shall appoint individuals within its organisation to be responsible for archives.

R3-039.doc: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 on clinical trials on medicinal products for human use, OJ L 158, 27.5.2014 (page reference); wording read in EUR-Lex consolidated text 02014R0536-20221205 (05.12.2022)
R3-039.paraphrase: Sixth (unnumbered) paragraph: any alteration to the content of the master file must be traceable. The third paragraph requires any transfer of ownership of the content to be documented.
R3-039.quote: Any alteration to the content of the clinical trial master file shall be traceable.
R3-039.record: audit trail of master file changes

R3-043.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-043.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-043.paraphrase: The glossary defines a serious breach as any deviation from the approved protocol version or the clinical trial regulation that is likely to significantly affect participant safety or rights, or data reliability and robustness. There is no separate glossary entry for 'breach'.
R3-043.quote: Any deviation of the approved protocol version or the clinical trial regulation

R3-044.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-044.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-044.paraphrase: A suspected serious breach is an incident reported by investigators or service providers that the sponsor has not yet assessed as a serious breach. This defines the intermediate state between identification and sponsor classification.
R3-044.quote: has not yet been assessed by the sponsor to be a serious breach

R3-045.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-045.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-045.paraphrase: A delegated party is a service provider appointed by the sponsor through a written contract to perform the Art. 52 tasks, i.e. to assess incidents that could be suspected serious breaches and/or report them to CTIS on behalf of the sponsor; delegation does not remove the ultimate responsibility of the sponsor or investigator for trial conduct.
R3-045.quote: does not remove the ultimate responsibility of the sponsor

R3-046.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-046.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-046.paraphrase: A service provider is a contracted party with delegated trial duties (other than the delegated party or investigator) that may observe a breach and must pass it on; examples include CROs, IRT vendors and IMP manufacturing sites.

R3-047.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-047.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-047.paraphrase: The sponsor is responsible for the serious breach notification via the EU portal / CTIS and may delegate the task to a service provider by written agreement as described in EU CTR Art. 71, while keeping responsibility.
R3-047.quote: may delegate this task to a service provider

R3-048.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-048.deadline: without undue delay and at the latest within 7 calendar days of the sponsor becoming aware
R3-048.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-048.paraphrase: The notification is due without undue delay and at the latest within 7 calendar days of the sponsor becoming aware; the sponsor should perform any assessment needed to confirm seriousness in a timely manner, and that assessment should not extend the 7-day period (the 7-day limit itself is binding through EU CTR Art. 52(1)).
R3-048.quote: within 7 calendar days of the sponsor becoming aware of a serious breach

R3-049.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-049.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-049.paraphrase: Where the sponsor has reasonable, evidence-based grounds to believe a serious breach occurred, it should notify first and continue investigating in parallel, without waiting for all details.
R3-049.quote: should not wait to obtain all of the details

R3-050.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-050.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-050.paraphrase: Only breaches the sponsor has assessed as serious are notified in CTIS; suspected serious breaches are not notified as such. The sponsor classification is the gate before the authority message flow.
R3-050.quote: only serious breaches must be notified, not suspected serious breaches

R3-051.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-051.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-051.paraphrase: Written contracts should require all parties to immediately report events that might meet the serious breach definition to the sponsor's designated contact point; for the principal investigator the protocol can serve as the written agreement.
R3-051.quote: immediately report any events that might meet the definition of a serious breach

R3-052.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-052.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-052.paraphrase: The sponsor should give the principal investigator a dedicated contact (e-mail and phone) for reporting, and the training of the PI and site staff on serious breach reporting should be documented, with training records kept in the clinical trial master file.
R3-052.quote: should be kept in the clinical trial master file (CTMF)

R3-053.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-053.deadline: as stated in the initial report (projected timelines)
R3-053.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-053.paraphrase: Updates can be made whenever further information becomes available. If investigation or CAPA is still ongoing, the initial report may give plans with projected completion timelines and should state when and what follow-up reports will be submitted through CTIS; S4 asks sponsors to update the CTIS fields and/or submit a follow-up report as new information arises. No fixed follow-up deadline is set.

R3-054.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-054.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-054.paraphrase: Breaches occurring exclusively outside the EU/EEA that are likely to affect an authorised or ongoing EU/EEA trial should be notified to the Member States concerned via CTIS under Art. 52.
R3-054.quote: should be notified to the MSC via the CTIS

R3-055.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-055.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-055.paraphrase: With a serious breach the sponsor should also consider whether other notifications are needed, e.g. unexpected events (Art. 53), urgent safety measures (Art. 54) or substantial modifications after a temporary halt or early termination (Art. 37, 38). S2 states that the guideline itself does not cover Art. 53 and 54 notifications.

R3-056.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-056.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-056.paraphrase: The sponsor completes the relevant CTIS fields (template in Appendix III a) and is encouraged to upload a detailed report covering the Appendix III b topics.
R3-056.record: CTIS structured fields; Appendix III b report
verify_raw: [verify] Appendix III a form content not in the text layer (local copy also empty; form is an image or form object)

R3-057.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-057.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-057.paraphrase: The sponsor indicates the most affected Member State in the notification title following the S4 diagram, with details in Appendix III b (A.7): a trial authorised in one Member State only makes that State the most affected; otherwise the questions are whether only one Member State is affected, whether the breach occurred in a specific Member State, and which Member State has most participants; if none applies, 'No most affected MS' is stated in the title.
R3-057.quote: indicate which is the Member State most affected

R3-058.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-058.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-058.paraphrase: Whether a breach significantly affects data reliability depends on factors such as trial design, the type and extent of affected data, their contribution to key analyses and the impact of excluding them. These are CtQ-like assessment criteria.

R3-059.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-059.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-059.paraphrase: Corrective or remedial actions taken do not change the fact that a breach occurred; mitigation is not a reason to skip classification or notification. Systematic or significant mis-dosing meets the criteria whether or not adverse reactions occurred.
R3-059.quote: do not negate the fact that a breach occurred

R3-060.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-060.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-060.paraphrase: It is the sponsor's responsibility to perform a thorough root cause analysis and to assess the impact of the breach on data reliability and robustness and on participant safety and/or rights; this assessment should be documented, as the sponsor's decisions may be examined later, e.g. during GCP inspections.

R3-061.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-061.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-061.paraphrase: If a delegated party disagrees with the sponsor and no notification follows, the communication and each party's position should be documented, together with the sponsor's reasons for not notifying.
R3-061.quote: the sponsor’s reasons for not proceeding with the notification

R3-062.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-062.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-062.paraphrase: An important deviation as defined by ICH E3 (Q&A R1) is not equivalent to a serious breach: one does not imply the other, and not every important deviation needs to be reported through CTIS as a serious breach. Two separate classification decisions are needed.
R3-062.quote: an important deviation is not necessarily also a serious breach and vice versa

R3-063.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-063.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-063.paraphrase: All serious breaches should be included in the corresponding clinical study report.
R3-063.quote: all serious breaches should be included in the corresponding clinical study report

R3-064.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-064.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-064.paraphrase: Deviations considered important under ICH E3 should be described in the CSR even if they are not serious breaches, because they may affect the data analysis.

R3-065.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-065.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-065.paraphrase: Deviations that do not significantly affect participant safety or rights or data reliability should still be documented, for example in the case report form or the clinical trial master file, so that corrective and preventive actions can be taken.
R3-065.record: case report form or clinical trial master file
verify_notes: The EMA serious breach guideline does not name who documents deviations that are not serious breaches; the step is shown in the Sponsor lane.
verify_raw: [verify] documenting party not named in the text

R3-066.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-066.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-066.paraphrase: The sponsor should have a formal process covering serious breach notification: suspected serious breaches are promptly reported to it by investigators and service providers, and management of serious breaches is part of the sponsor's quality system as a specific SOP and/or written in the protocol. Lack of an adequate system or failure to report may result in GCP inspection findings.
R3-066.quote: There should be a formal process in place

R3-067.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-067.deadline: within the 7 calendar day notification window for the assessment
R3-067.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-067.paraphrase: After receipt, the sponsor assesses whether the breach is serious (deviations/violations, isolated or systematic incidents, participants harmed or put at risk, data credibility) and investigates it, including a root cause analysis that may still be ongoing at the time of reporting.

R3-068.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-068.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-068.paraphrase: Corrective and preventive actions should be identified as part of the sponsor's serious breach process.
R3-068.quote: corrective and preventive actions should be identified

R3-069.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-069.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-069.paraphrase: A delegated party carries out the sponsor tasks of S6.1 under written contract and keeps the sponsor informed about the management of all breaches in the sponsor's trials.
R3-069.quote: keeps the sponsor informed about the management of all the breaches

R3-070.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-070.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-070.paraphrase: Service providers should have a written process to identify suspected serious breaches and promptly communicate them to the sponsor or delegated party, using the contact details provided and per contract.
R3-070.quote: should have a written process in place to identify

R3-071.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG); no EU CTR article imposes this investigator duty
R3-071.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-071.paraphrase: The principal investigator should have a process (formal SOP or study-specific guidance) ensuring that site staff and service providers delegated by the PI/institution can identify suspected serious breaches and that these are promptly reported to the sponsor or delegated party through the contacts provided.
R3-071.quote: a (suspected) serious breach is promptly reported to the sponsor or delegated party

R3-072.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-072.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-072.paraphrase: All concerns about potential fraud in clinical trials that the sponsor becomes aware of are expected to be reported as serious breaches; national criminal law applies in addition.
R3-072.quote: all concerns about potential cases of fraud in clinical trials

R3-073.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-073.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-073.paraphrase: The party where the breach occurred should verify its impact on other ongoing or ended clinical trials it is involved in.
R3-073.party: The party (e.g. sponsor, CRO, investigator) at which the serious breach occurred
R3-073.quote: should verify the impact of the breach on other clinical trials

R3-074.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-074.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-074.paraphrase: A breach (e.g. mis-dosing from an error) that may result in an SAE or SUSAR can be a serious breach, and failure to manage safety events (e.g. lack of SUSAR reporting) that puts participants at significant risk is a serious breach to be reported; this does not exempt the sponsor from Art. 53/54 notifications or EudraVigilance SUSAR submission.

R3-075.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-075.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-075.paraphrase: Persistent or systematic non-compliance with the Regulation, including deviation from GCP principles or the protocol as described in Art. 47, constitutes a serious breach when it is likely to significantly affect the safety and rights of a participant in the EU/EEA or the reliability and robustness of the trial data. Recurring or trended deviations can therefore escalate to a serious breach.
R3-075.quote: is likely to significantly affect the safety and rights of a trial participant

R3-076.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-076.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-076.paraphrase: A serious breach at a single site, inside or outside the EU/EEA, should also be notified where it leads to removal of data from the trial analysis.
R3-076.quote: this leads to the removal of data from the trial analysis

R3-077.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-077.deadline: none (no assessment timeline set in law, per CTIS-BT-SB24 slide 29)
R3-077.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-077.paraphrase: Member States assess notified serious breaches in the CTIS secure module; the assessment leads to publication of the breach and its evaluation in the CTIS public domain. Some breaches are managed in-house through acceptable CAPA under Member State oversight; others may trigger an (urgent) inspection, published together with the inspection report, or regulatory action.
R3-077.quote: managed in-house via acceptable Corrective and Preventive Actions

R3-078.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline restating EU CTR Art. 77
R3-078.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-078.paraphrase: Before imposing corrective measures under EU CTR Art. 77 (e.g. suspension or revocation), the MSC asks the sponsor for an opinion, due within 7 days, except where immediate action is required.
R3-078.quote: the MSC will ask the sponsor for their opinion

R3-079.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-079.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-079.paraphrase: Example judged a serious breach: a site repeatedly failed, for several subjects over a year and despite monitor findings, to reduce or stop trial medication after abnormal laboratory values as the protocol required. Shows persistence after monitoring escalation as a seriousness factor.

R3-080.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-080.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-080.paraphrase: Example judged not a serious breach: a common, minor visit date deviation is a minor protocol deviation that does not meet the notification criteria; a major visit date deviation (8.3) can be serious depending on its safety or data impact.
R3-080.quote: a minor protocol deviation, which does not meet the criteria for notification

R3-081.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-081.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-081.paraphrase: Points to consider (bulleted list, not a decision tree): decide whether the breach meets the Art. 52 definition and, if likely significant, regard and report it as serious during the investigation; a proper quality management system should identify the root cause, evaluate the extent and, for a systematic breach, whether other subjects or trials are affected, establish whether human error, lack of training or failure to follow a procedure caused it, and for service-provider causes check the sponsor's other open or closed trials with that provider.

R3-082.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-082.deadline: CAPA timelines reasonable for the breach
R3-082.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-082.paraphrase: The CAPA plan should protect affected subjects or data reliability, consider suspending or terminating the trial or removing affected data from the CSR, prevent recurrence (procedure updates, training, system changes) and have timelines proportionate to the breach.

R3-083.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-083.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-083.paraphrase: Where subject safety or rights were compromised, the sponsor should take proportionate actions, which may include informing the affected subjects.

R3-084.binding_route: EU: non-binding guideline (CTFG and GCP IWG), implements EU CTR Art. 52
R3-084.doc: Guideline for the notification of serious breaches of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 or the clinical trial protocol, EMA/698382/2021, document date 30 June 2023, effective 31 January 2022
R3-084.paraphrase: Information submitted with a notification (mandatory CTIS fields plus free text or uploaded document) covers: A general information (investigation status and next follow-up date, trial title and type, regulatory procedure, other trials impacted with EU CT number, site details, most affected Member State), B breach details (description, potential impact with sub-category, other details) and C actions (impact assessment with methodology, root cause investigation, CAPA plan with owner, timeline, status and how the incident is documented in the TMF, actual impact). Where C details are not yet known, the report states when they will follow.

R3-085.binding_route: EU: Commission/CTAG Q&A (non-binding) interpreting EU CTR; ICH GCP subordinate to EU CTR where they conflict
R3-085.doc: Clinical Trials Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 Questions & Answers, EudraLex Volume 10, version 7.4, October 2026 (supersedes 7.3)
R3-085.page: printed 4-5 (chapter 1; page numbers restart per chapter)
R3-085.paraphrase: Q&A 1.5: sponsors and investigators must comply with applicable regulatory requirements; the EU CTR aims at maximum harmonisation and takes precedence over conflicting rules in guidelines, including ICH GCP. Documents or data not foreseen by the Regulation (e.g. the ICH E6 progress report) shall not be requested or submitted on the basis of recommendations in other guidelines.
R3-085.quote: takes precedence over conflicting rules in guidelines

R3-086.binding_route: EU: Commission/CTAG Q&A (non-binding) interpreting EU CTR
R3-086.doc: Clinical Trials Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 Questions & Answers, EudraLex Volume 10, version 7.4, October 2026 (supersedes 7.3)
R3-086.page: printed 4-5 (chapter 1; page numbers restart per chapter)
R3-086.paraphrase: Q&A 1.5: all submissions for a trial, including site information, are made by or on behalf of the sponsor, not the investigator, via CTIS or EudraVigilance. Investigators therefore do not notify authorities directly under the EU CTR.

R3-090.binding_route: EU: EMA training material (non-binding) on implementing EU CTR Art. 52 in CTIS
R3-090.doc: CTIS Bitesize Talk: End of transition period and notifications including serious breaches, EMA, 16 October 2024 (presentation)
R3-090.page: slide 20; notification type label on an unnumbered CTCG slide
R3-090.paraphrase: For trials authorised in the EU/EEA, a serious breach is reported via CTIS to all Member States concerned regardless of where it occurred; the notification type is 'Serious Breaches, safety relevant (SB)'.
R3-090.quote: the SB should be reported via CTIS to all MSC

R3-091.binding_route: EU: EMA training material (non-binding) on implementing EU CTR Art. 52 in CTIS
R3-091.doc: CTIS Bitesize Talk: End of transition period and notifications including serious breaches, EMA, 16 October 2024 (presentation)
R3-091.page: slides 20, 26, 28; EU CT number point on an unnumbered CTCG slide
R3-091.paraphrase: The sponsor fills all mandatory structured fields (Appendix III a); a free-text entry or uploaded document (Appendix III b, highly recommended) supplements but does not replace them. CTIS has no field for the most affected Member State, so it goes in the structured fields or the report; if missing, the reporting Member State asks by RFI. Other trials affected by the same issue are listed by EU CT number.

R3-092.binding_route: EU: EMA training material (non-binding) on implementing EU CTR Art. 52 in CTIS
R3-092.doc: CTIS Bitesize Talk: End of transition period and notifications including serious breaches, EMA, 16 October 2024 (presentation)
R3-092.paraphrase: The serious breach report can be updated as the investigation progresses, and a fuller CAPA can be provided after full investigation.
R3-092.quote: Updates to the SB report can be made

R3-094.binding_route: EU: EMA training material (non-binding) on CTIS transparency for EU CTR Art. 52 notifications
R3-094.doc: CTIS Bitesize Talk: End of transition period and notifications including serious breaches, EMA, 16 October 2024 (presentation)
R3-094.paraphrase: Serious breach, USM and unexpected event notifications are published only after the Member State assessment is finalised in CTIS (for Category 1 trials in adults: 30 months after EU/EEA end of trial and MSC assessment). Only sponsor-entered structured data are published, no authority-entered data and no notification documents; a serious breach withdrawn at Member State request is not published.
R3-094.quote: The notification is published only once the Member State assessment is finalized in CTIS

R3-095.binding_route: EU: EMA CTIS training material (non-binding), authority-side handling
R3-095.doc: Supervise a CT - Ad Hoc Assessment: FAQs, CTIS Training Programme Module 17, version 1.3, August 2024 (EMA)
R3-095.paraphrase: Member States may create an ad hoc assessment in CTIS linked to serious breach, urgent safety measure or unexpected event notifications; the outcome is informative only and a change of trial status requires a recommended action such as a corrective measure. Sponsors take part only if RFIs are raised.
R3-095.party: MSs (represented by NCAs and Ethics Committees)

R3-096.binding_route: EU: EMA CTIS training material (non-binding), authority-side handling
R3-096.doc: Supervise a CT - Ad Hoc Assessment: FAQs, CTIS Training Programme Module 17, version 1.3, August 2024 (EMA)
R3-096.paraphrase: When finalising, the Member State links the assessment conclusion to the notification or selects 'no Ad-hoc assessment required'; either action publishes the notification details on the CTIS public portal.

R3-097.binding_route: EU: EMA CTIS training material (non-binding); 2021 version, UI may have changed
R3-097.doc: How to manage a clinical trial - step-by-step guide, CTIS Training Programme Module 05, version 1.0, October 2021 (EMA)
R3-097.paraphrase: Other notification types are created in the trial's 'Notifications' sub-tab via '+ New', completed and submitted; a submitted notification can be viewed, updated or withdrawn, and an update or withdrawal requires a justification. Example given is an unexpected event; serious breaches are not mentioned.
verify_notes: CTIS screen details for updating a notification come from EMA training material; the current CTIS sponsor handbook section on notifications could not be read.

R3-098.binding_route: EU: Commission/CTAG Q&A (non-binding) interpreting EU CTR
R3-098.deadline: within seven days of becoming aware of the potential breach
R3-098.doc: Clinical Trials Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 Questions & Answers, EudraLex Volume 10, version 7.4, October 2026 (supersedes 7.3)
R3-098.paraphrase: Q&A 11.3 (point 523): the 7-day timeframe of Art. 52(1) starts when the sponsor becomes aware of a potential breach; only confirmed serious breaches are reported, so the sponsor completes its first analysis, confirms seriousness and submits the initial report in CTIS within those 7 days.
R3-098.quote: The 7-day timeframe starts when the sponsor becomes aware of a potential breach.

R3-099.binding_route: EU: Commission/CTAG Q&A (non-binding) interpreting EU CTR
R3-099.doc: Clinical Trials Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 Questions & Answers, EudraLex Volume 10, version 7.4, October 2026 (supersedes 7.3)
R3-099.paraphrase: Q&A 11.3 (point 522): a serious breach identified at a site outside the EU/EEA that is likely to affect the safety and rights of EU/EEA subjects and/or the reliability and robustness of the trial data requires notification to the EU/EEA.

R3-100.binding_route: EU: Commission/CTAG Q&A (non-binding) interpreting EU CTR
R3-100.doc: Clinical Trials Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 Questions & Answers, EudraLex Volume 10, version 7.4, October 2026 (supersedes 7.3)
R3-100.paraphrase: Q&A 10.9 (points 498-499): urgent safety measures may involve a temporary halt for safety reasons; one notification is sufficient. If the entire trial is halted (recruitment and/or treatment) a temporary halt notification is submitted; if only parts are halted (e.g. arms, groups, subprotocols) it is reported as an urgent safety measure so that the trial status stays 'ongoing' in CTIS.

R3-101.binding_route: EU: Commission/CTAG Q&A (non-binding) interpreting EU CTR
R3-101.deadline: without undue delay but not later than seven days from the date the measures have been taken
R3-101.doc: Clinical Trials Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 Questions & Answers, EudraLex Volume 10, version 7.4, October 2026 (supersedes 7.3)
R3-101.paraphrase: Q&A 10.9 (point 500): the reporting timelines for temporary halts and USMs must be kept; a temporary halt notification accompanied by additional urgent safety measures is due without undue delay and not later than seven days from the date the measures were taken (Art. 54), i.e. the shorter USM clock applies instead of the 15 days of Art. 38(1).

R3-102.binding_route: EU: Commission/CTAG Q&A (non-binding) interpreting EU CTR
R3-102.doc: Clinical Trials Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 Questions & Answers, EudraLex Volume 10, version 7.4, October 2026 (supersedes 7.3)
R3-102.paraphrase: Q&A 10.1 overview table maps events to CTIS notification types and legal bases: serious breach = SB (Art. 52(1), see EMA-SB); unexpected events affecting benefit-risk, except SUSARs = UE (Art. 53(1)); unexpected events where the sponsor or investigator has taken urgent safety measures = USM (Art. 54(2)), also used for a partial temporary halt or a decision to early terminate (parts of) a trial for benefit-risk reasons; temporary halt or early termination of the whole trial for benefit-risk reasons = TH / ET (Art. 38(1)); restart = substantial modification (Art. 38(2)); third-country inspection reports = TI (Art. 53(2)).

R3-103.binding_route: EU: Commission/CTAG Q&A (non-binding) interpreting EU CTR
R3-103.deadline: USM: not later than 7 days from the date the measures have been taken; SM: not stated
R3-103.doc: Clinical Trials Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 Questions & Answers, EudraLex Volume 10, version 7.4, October 2026 (supersedes 7.3)
R3-103.paraphrase: Q&A 7.27 (point 368): where an urgent safety measure requires a protocol update, the USM is notified immediately (and within 7 days of the measures) to inform of applied and/or planned changes, and must then be followed by submission of the documents as a substantial modification for approval.

R3-104.binding_route: EU: Commission/CTAG Q&A (non-binding) interpreting EU CTR
R3-104.doc: Clinical Trials Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 Questions & Answers, EudraLex Volume 10, version 7.4, October 2026 (supersedes 7.3)
R3-104.paraphrase: Q&A 7.27 (points 365-367): safety notifications are made via CTIS; when submitting a USM, unexpected event, temporary halt or premature end notification, sponsors inform the Member States whether other trials are affected, list their EU CT numbers, state whether the same or similar notification is or will be submitted for them, and provide available documents and proposed risk minimisation measures where possible.
R3-104.record: table of affected EU CT numbers

R3-106.binding_route: EU: EMA training material (non-binding) on implementing EU CTR Art. 52 in CTIS
R3-106.doc: CTIS Bitesize Talk: End of transition period and notifications including serious breaches, EMA, 16 October 2024 (presentation)
R3-106.paraphrase: If a Member State assesses that a notified serious breach should not have been submitted as such, it asks the sponsor through an ad hoc assessment RFI to withdraw it; the sponsor should withdraw a submitted serious breach only on such a Member State request, and the withdrawn breach is not published.

R3-107.binding_route: EU: EMA training material (non-binding) on implementing EU CTR Art. 52 in CTIS
R3-107.doc: CTIS Bitesize Talk: End of transition period and notifications including serious breaches, EMA, 16 October 2024 (presentation)
R3-107.paraphrase: Whether an incident qualifies as a serious breach depends on trial and incident factors and is judged case by case; reporting incidents that are not real serious breaches burdens assessors and should be avoided.

R4-004.binding_route: US: federal regulation (21 CFR), legally binding for clinical investigations of drugs under an IND; EU: not applicable
R4-004.doc: 21 CFR Part 312 - Investigational New Drug Application, section 312.30 Protocol amendments (eCFR, up to date as of 10/22/2026)
R4-004.page: n/a - eCFR web text without pagination
R4-004.paraphrase: As an exception to (b)(2)(i), a protocol change intended to eliminate an apparent immediate hazard to subjects may be implemented at once, without waiting for FDA submission or IRB approval. The paragraph is passive; 312.30 as a whole is addressed to the IND sponsor.

R4-005.binding_route: US: federal regulation (21 CFR), legally binding for clinical investigations of drugs under an IND; EU: not applicable
R4-005.deadline: FDA: subsequently, no period stated; IRB: per 21CFR56.104(c) cross-reference [verify whether its 5-working-day window applies]
R4-005.doc: 21 CFR Part 312 - Investigational New Drug Application, section 312.30 Protocol amendments (eCFR, up to date as of 10/22/2026)
R4-005.page: n/a - eCFR web text without pagination
R4-005.paraphrase: The immediate-hazard exception applies provided FDA is notified afterwards by a protocol amendment and the reviewing IRB is notified in accordance with 21 CFR 56.104(c). No period is stated for the FDA amendment; 56.104(c) itself sets a 5-working-day reporting window for emergency use of a test article.
verify: Deadline not settled: 21 CFR 312.30 requires IRB notification of immediate-hazard protocol changes per 21 CFR 56.104(c); it does not say whether the 5-working-day window applies.
