R4-007.binding_route: US: federal regulation (21 CFR), legally binding for clinical investigations of drugs under an IND; EU: not applicable
R4-007.doc: 21 CFR Part 312 - Investigational New Drug Application, section 312.50 General responsibilities of sponsors (eCFR, up to date as of 10/08/2026)
R4-007.page: n/a - eCFR web text without pagination
R4-007.paraphrase: Sponsors are responsible for ensuring proper monitoring of the investigation(s). Section 312.50 is a single unnumbered paragraph.

R4-008.binding_route: US: federal regulation (21 CFR), legally binding for clinical investigations of drugs under an IND; EU: not applicable
R4-008.doc: 21 CFR Part 312 - Investigational New Drug Application, section 312.50 General responsibilities of sponsors (eCFR, up to date as of 10/08/2026)
R4-008.page: n/a - eCFR web text without pagination
R4-008.paraphrase: Sponsors are responsible for ensuring that each investigation is conducted in accordance with the general investigational plan and the protocols contained in the IND - the regulatory anchor for sponsor oversight of protocol compliance (FDA-PD24 SIII.B.2 lines 220-222 restates this).

R4-009.binding_route: US: federal regulation (21 CFR), legally binding for clinical investigations of drugs under an IND; EU: not applicable
R4-009.doc: 21 CFR Part 312 - Investigational New Drug Application, section 312.50 General responsibilities of sponsors (eCFR, up to date as of 10/08/2026)
R4-009.page: n/a - eCFR web text without pagination
R4-009.paraphrase: Sponsors are responsible for ensuring that FDA and all participating investigators are promptly informed of significant new adverse effects or risks with respect to the drug.

R4-010.binding_route: US: federal regulation (21 CFR), legally binding for clinical investigations of drugs under an IND; commitment made binding through the signed Form FDA-1572; EU: not applicable
R4-010.deadline: before the change (exception: protection of subject safety, rights or welfare)
R4-010.doc: 21 CFR Part 312 - Investigational New Drug Application, section 312.53 Selecting investigators and monitors (eCFR, up to date as of 10/23/2026)
R4-010.page: n/a - eCFR web text without pagination
R4-010.paraphrase: In the signed investigator statement (Form FDA-1572) the investigator commits to conduct the study according to the relevant current protocol and to make protocol changes only after notifying the sponsor, except where needed to protect the safety, rights or welfare of subjects. This is the binding US basis for investigator-to-sponsor communication on changes; 312.56(b) makes noncompliance with this agreement a sponsor trigger.

R4-011.binding_route: US: federal regulation (21 CFR), legally binding for clinical investigations of drugs under an IND; commitment made binding through the signed Form FDA-1572; EU: not applicable
R4-011.doc: 21 CFR Part 312 - Investigational New Drug Application, section 312.53 Selecting investigators and monitors (eCFR, up to date as of 10/23/2026)
R4-011.page: n/a - eCFR web text without pagination
R4-011.paraphrase: For studies subject to Part 56, the investigator commits in Form FDA-1572 that a Part 56 IRB will handle initial and continuing review, that all changes in the research activity and all unanticipated problems involving risks are promptly reported to the IRB, and that no changes are made without IRB approval except to eliminate apparent immediate hazards. Mirrors 312.66.

R4-012.binding_route: US: federal regulation (21 CFR), legally binding for clinical investigations of drugs under an IND; EU: not applicable
R4-012.doc: 21 CFR Part 312 - Investigational New Drug Application, section 312.56 Review of ongoing investigations (eCFR, up to date as of 10/19/2026)
R4-012.page: n/a - eCFR web text without pagination
R4-012.paraphrase: The sponsor has to monitor the progress of all clinical investigations conducted under its IND.

R4-013.binding_route: US: federal regulation (21 CFR), legally binding for clinical investigations of drugs under an IND; EU: not applicable
R4-013.doc: 21 CFR Part 312 - Investigational New Drug Application, section 312.56 Review of ongoing investigations (eCFR, up to date as of 10/19/2026)
R4-013.page: n/a - eCFR web text without pagination
R4-013.paraphrase: A sponsor that discovers an investigator is not complying with the signed agreement (Form FDA-1572), the general investigational plan, or Part 312 or other applicable parts has to promptly either secure compliance or stop drug shipments to that investigator and end the investigator's participation.

R4-014.binding_route: US: federal regulation (21 CFR), legally binding for clinical investigations of drugs under an IND; EU: not applicable
R4-014.doc: 21 CFR Part 312 - Investigational New Drug Application, section 312.56 Review of ongoing investigations (eCFR, up to date as of 10/19/2026)
R4-014.page: n/a - eCFR web text without pagination
R4-014.paraphrase: If an investigator's participation is ended for noncompliance, the sponsor has to require the investigator to dispose of or return the investigational drug under 312.59 and has to notify FDA.

R4-017.binding_route: US: federal regulation (21 CFR), legally binding for clinical investigations of drugs under an IND; EU: not applicable
R4-017.doc: 21 CFR Part 312 - Investigational New Drug Application, section 312.60 General responsibilities of investigators (eCFR, up to date as of 10/23/2026)
R4-017.page: n/a - eCFR web text without pagination
R4-017.paraphrase: The investigator is responsible for ensuring that the investigation is conducted according to the signed investigator statement, the investigational plan and applicable regulations. Section 312.60 is a single unnumbered paragraph.

R4-018.binding_route: US: federal regulation (21 CFR), legally binding for clinical investigations of drugs under an IND; EU: not applicable
R4-018.doc: 21 CFR Part 312 - Investigational New Drug Application, section 312.60 General responsibilities of investigators (eCFR, up to date as of 10/23/2026)
R4-018.page: n/a - eCFR web text without pagination
R4-018.paraphrase: The investigator is responsible for protecting the rights, safety and welfare of subjects under the investigator's care and for control of the drugs under investigation. FDA-PD24 SIII.B.1 (lines 190-194) notes that failing to follow protocol elements designed to protect subjects may be considered a failure of this duty.

R4-019.binding_route: US: federal regulation (21 CFR), legally binding for clinical investigations of drugs under an IND; EU: not applicable
R4-019.doc: 21 CFR Part 312 - Investigational New Drug Application, section 312.60 General responsibilities of investigators (eCFR, up to date as of 10/23/2026)
R4-019.page: n/a - eCFR web text without pagination
R4-019.paraphrase: The investigator has to obtain the informed consent of each human subject to whom the drug is administered, in accordance with Part 50. Basis for consent-related deviations (FDA-PD24 lists failure to obtain consent as an important deviation).

R4-020.binding_route: US: federal regulation (21 CFR), legally binding for clinical investigations of drugs under an IND; EU: not applicable
R4-020.doc: 21 CFR Part 312 - Investigational New Drug Application, section 312.62 Investigator recordkeeping and record retention (eCFR, up to date as of 10/21/2026)
R4-020.page: n/a - eCFR web text without pagination
R4-020.paraphrase: The investigator has to prepare and maintain adequate and accurate case histories recording all observations and other relevant data for each subject given the drug or used as a control, including case report forms and supporting data such as signed and dated consent forms and medical records; the case history has to document that consent was obtained before participation. This is the binding source-record basis on which deviations are identified and documented at site.
R4-020.record: case histories: case report forms, consent forms, medical records (progress notes, hospital charts, nursing notes)

R4-021.binding_route: US: federal regulation (21 CFR), legally binding for clinical investigations of drugs under an IND; EU: not applicable
R4-021.deadline: 2 years after approval, or 2 years after discontinuation and FDA notification
R4-021.doc: 21 CFR Part 312 - Investigational New Drug Application, section 312.62 Investigator recordkeeping and record retention (eCFR, up to date as of 10/21/2026)
R4-021.page: n/a - eCFR web text without pagination
R4-021.paraphrase: The investigator has to retain the required records for 2 years after a marketing application is approved for the indication investigated, or, if no application is filed or it is not approved for that indication, for 2 years after the investigation is discontinued and FDA is notified.

R4-022.binding_route: US: federal regulation (21 CFR), legally binding for clinical investigations of drugs under an IND; EU: not applicable
R4-022.doc: 21 CFR Part 312 - Investigational New Drug Application, section 312.66 Assurance of IRB review (eCFR, up to date as of 10/21/2026)
R4-022.page: n/a - eCFR web text without pagination
R4-022.paraphrase: The investigator has to assure that an IRB complying with Part 56 will be responsible for initial and continuing review and approval of the proposed study. Section 312.66 is a single unnumbered paragraph.

R4-023.binding_route: US: federal regulation (21 CFR), legally binding for clinical investigations of drugs under an IND; EU: not applicable
R4-023.doc: 21 CFR Part 312 - Investigational New Drug Application, section 312.66 Assurance of IRB review (eCFR, up to date as of 10/21/2026)
R4-023.page: n/a - eCFR web text without pagination
R4-023.paraphrase: The investigator has to assure that he or she will promptly report to the IRB all changes in the research activity and all unanticipated problems involving risks to human subjects or others.

R4-024.binding_route: US: federal regulation (21 CFR), legally binding for clinical investigations of drugs under an IND; EU: not applicable
R4-024.doc: 21 CFR Part 312 - Investigational New Drug Application, section 312.66 Assurance of IRB review (eCFR, up to date as of 10/21/2026)
R4-024.page: n/a - eCFR web text without pagination
R4-024.paraphrase: The investigator will not make any change in the research without IRB approval, except where necessary to eliminate apparent immediate hazards to human subjects. FDA-PD24 applies this to intentional single-participant deviations (prior IRB approval required).
R4-024.quote: except where necessary to eliminate apparent immediate hazards to human subjects

R4-026.binding_route: US: federal regulation (21 CFR), legally binding for IRBs reviewing FDA-regulated research; EU: not applicable
R4-026.doc: 21 CFR Part 56 - Institutional Review Boards, section 56.108 IRB functions and operations (eCFR, up to date as of 10/20/2026)
R4-026.page: n/a - eCFR web text without pagination
R4-026.paraphrase: Each IRB has to follow written procedures ensuring that changes in approved research, during the period of approval, are not initiated without IRB review and approval, except where necessary to eliminate apparent immediate hazards to the subjects.

R4-028.binding_route: US: federal regulation (21 CFR), legally binding for IRBs reviewing FDA-regulated research; EU: not applicable
R4-028.doc: 21 CFR Part 56 - Institutional Review Boards, section 56.108 IRB functions and operations (eCFR, up to date as of 10/20/2026)
R4-028.page: n/a - eCFR web text without pagination
R4-028.paraphrase: Each IRB has to follow written procedures for ensuring prompt reporting to the IRB, appropriate institutional officials and FDA of any instance of serious or continuing noncompliance with the FDA regulations or with the IRB's requirements or determinations.

R4-030.binding_route: US: federal regulation (21 CFR), legally binding for FDA-regulated research; EU: not applicable
R4-030.doc: 21 CFR Part 56 - Institutional Review Boards, section 56.104 Exemptions from IRB requirement (Cornell LII rendering of current CFR, read 2026-11-06)
R4-030.paraphrase: Emergency use of a test article is exempt from prior IRB review provided the emergency use is reported to the IRB within 5 working days; any later use of the test article at the institution is subject to IRB review. Relevant here only because 21CFR312.30(b)(2)(ii) cross-refers to it for IRB notification of immediate-hazard protocol changes.
R4-030.party: not named (passive: emergency use is reported to the IRB)
R4-030.quote: reported to the IRB within 5 working days
verify_raw: eCFR text of 56.104(c) not retrievable (robots); confirm against eCFR or govinfo before X1

R4-035.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); definition adopted from ICH E3(R1) Q&A; no binding US definition exists in 21 CFR; EU: not applicable
R4-035.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-035.paraphrase: FDA notes that its regulations neither define protocol deviation nor classify deviation types (SI lines 17-19), and adopts the ICH E3(R1) Q&A definition: a protocol deviation is any change, divergence or departure from the study design or procedures defined in the protocol.
R4-035.quote: any change, divergence, or departure from the study design or procedures

R4-036.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); definition adopted from ICH E3(R1) Q&A; EU: not applicable
R4-036.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-036.paraphrase: An important protocol deviation is the subset of protocol deviations that might significantly affect the completeness, accuracy or reliability of study data, or a subject's rights, safety or well-being (adopted from ICH E3(R1)).
R4-036.quote: a subset of protocol deviations that might significantly affect the completeness

R4-037.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-037.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-037.paraphrase: Deviations are usually unintended and often found after the fact; an intentional one-off departure for a single participant (example: enrolling a participant above the maximum age with sponsor and IRB approval) should be extremely rare because the protocol should provide appropriate flexibility.
R4-037.party: not named (protocol design; sponsor role per SIII.B.2)

R4-038.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-038.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-038.paraphrase: FDA does not regard every GCP compliance issue as a protocol deviation, particularly where the protocol does not specify the detail (example: a missing signature on a delegation log); counting such issues as deviations inflates numbers. They should be addressed, but outside the protocol deviation process.

R4-039.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-039.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-039.paraphrase: Deviations can be identified by site staff, study staff, site or central monitoring, audits and regulatory inspections, and may occur at participant level (missed visit), site level (product stored outside the required temperature range) or study level (premature unblinding).
R4-039.party: site staff, study staff, site or central monitoring, audits, regulatory inspections

R4-040.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-040.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-040.paraphrase: In premarket review FDA may weigh the number and types of deviations when judging data quality and interpretability; deviations leading to improper enrolment, monitoring or assessment, or to missing or inaccurate data, may lead FDA to conclude a study is not adequate and well-controlled. Rationale for complete identification and documentation.

R4-041.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-041.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-041.paraphrase: FDA recommends using the single term 'important' for deviations otherwise labelled major, critical or significant.
R4-041.party: not named (guidance audience: sponsors, investigators, IRBs)

R4-042.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); CtQ concept from ICH E8(R1); EU: not applicable
R4-042.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-042.paraphrase: Deviations classified as important should generally be those that could affect critical-to-quality factors (as in ICH E8(R1)), and deviations related to those factors should be identified; examples of such factors are accurate eligibility determination, randomization integrity and accurate endpoint data collection. Thoughtful protocol design can reduce important deviations.
R4-042.party: not named (protocol design; sponsor role per SIII.B.2)

R4-043.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-043.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-043.paraphrase: It may be helpful for the protocol to define important protocol deviations and to give study-specific examples.

R4-044.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-044.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-044.paraphrase: Non-exhaustive list of deviations FDA considers important because they affect subject protection or safety assessment: failure to perform safety assessments or adequately monitor participants (e.g. missing important safety labs, product not administered as specified); prohibited concomitant treatment raising risk; failure to obtain informed consent or meet Part 50; failure to protect identifiable private health information; failure to withdraw product when withdrawal criteria are met; wrong treatment, incorrect dose or wrong device; failure to follow the randomization scheme.

R4-045.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-045.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-045.paraphrase: Non-exhaustive list of important deviations that may reduce the reliability of effectiveness conclusions: enrolling participants in violation of key eligibility criteria defining the population; failure to collect data needed for important primary or secondary endpoints; premature unblinding for reasons not specified in the protocol.

R4-046.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-046.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-046.paraphrase: Deviations not meeting the important definition (sometimes called minor, non-critical or non-significant) include minor visit-window departures, a signed consent form missing a participant's initial, and a missed procedure that is neither safety-relevant nor tied to an important primary or secondary efficacy endpoint.

R4-047.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); related binding basis 21CFR312.53(c)(1)(vi)(a) covers prior notification of protocol changes only; EU: not applicable
R4-047.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-047.paraphrase: For drug investigations, investigators should report to the sponsor every protocol deviation they are aware of, using a process that flags the important ones.

R4-048.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, nonbinding) for prior sponsor approval; the IRB-approval part restates binding 21CFR312.66 (R4-024); EU: not applicable
R4-048.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-048.paraphrase: Where an investigator contemplates an intentional departure from the IRB-approved protocol for a single participant, the investigator should get prior sponsor approval and must get prior IRB approval (citing 312.66), unless urgently needed to eliminate apparent immediate hazards; such departures should be extremely rare.

R4-049.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-049.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-049.paraphrase: Sponsors should train investigators on the protocol to support adherence and on how to recognise important protocol deviations.

R4-050.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-050.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-050.paraphrase: Sponsors should focus planned oversight on critical trial activities to improve detection of important protocol deviations.

R4-051.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-051.deadline: promptly, during the trial where possible
R4-051.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-051.paraphrase: Where possible, important protocol deviations should be remedied or addressed promptly during the trial to reduce risk to participants and protect data quality.

R4-052.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-052.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-052.paraphrase: Sponsors should receive information on all protocol deviations, most likely through site monitoring and centralized monitoring.

R4-053.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-053.deadline: before trial start (pre-specification); updates during the trial
R4-053.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-053.paraphrase: The protocol should specify in advance which types of deviation will be considered important; the list may be updated as data accumulate during the trial.
R4-053.quote: pre-specify which types of protocol deviations will be considered important

R4-054.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-054.deadline: sponsor-defined; example: important deviations within x days of occurrence (x not specified), other deviations at site monitoring visits
R4-054.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-054.paraphrase: Sponsors should tell investigators the timeframe and method for reporting deviations; FDA's example is important deviations reported to the sponsor expeditiously within a sponsor-set number of days of occurrence, other deviations at site monitoring visits.
R4-054.record: deviation reporting instructions (e.g. protocol or plan)

R4-055.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); CSR structure from ICH E3; EU: not applicable
R4-055.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-055.paraphrase: Sponsors should discuss important protocol deviations in the body of clinical study reports submitted in an NDA or BLA. Footnote 16 adds that for CDER applications all deviations are to be provided as described in the Bioresearch Monitoring Technical Conformance Guide (v3.1, September 2024).
verify_raw: Exact wording and modal of footnote 16 (BIMO Technical Conformance Guide reference) not double-checked

R4-056.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); CSR structure from ICH E3; EU: not applicable
R4-056.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-056.paraphrase: The patient data listing in the CSR appendix should list all trial participants with important deviations by unique subject identifier, organised by site for multicenter studies (footnote 17 cites ICH E3).

R4-057.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); electronic study data submission requirements sit in FDA data standards documents not read here; EU: not applicable
R4-057.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-057.paraphrase: Sponsors should report all protocol deviations in the SDTM protocol deviation (DV) domain so FDA can assess their effect on data quality (footnote 18 cites the Study Data Technical Conformance Guide, October 2024).

R4-058.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-058.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-058.paraphrase: The DV domain should include a variable recording the sponsor's determination of whether each deviation is important.

R4-059.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, nonbinding) for the deviation note; the safety reports themselves are binding under 21CFR312.32 (not extracted in this stem); EU: not applicable
R4-059.deadline: with the safety report (clock per 21CFR312.32, not extracted)
R4-059.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-059.paraphrase: During the trial sponsors must already submit mandatory safety reports (for drugs, IND safety reports under 21 CFR 312.32); in such reports they should state when a protocol deviation contributed to the event, e.g. a safety lab not collected before a serious event. The guidance does not mention IND annual reports.

R4-060.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-060.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-060.paraphrase: For deviations not classified as important, sponsors should document and evaluate their types and numbers to decide whether reclassification as important is warranted, and if so notify the investigator of the reclassification.

R4-061.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); amendment itself binding under 21CFR312.30; EU: not applicable
R4-061.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-061.paraphrase: Sponsors should carefully consider investigators' requests for deviations to decide whether a protocol amendment is needed for consistent conduct across sites, and should build enough flexibility into the protocol that intentional deviations are unnecessary.
R4-061.record: decision on request; protocol amendment if needed

R4-062.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-062.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-062.paraphrase: Sponsors may prevent or reduce important deviations through quality by design (ICH E8(R1)): simpler and more flexible protocols, flexible and fewer enrolment criteria, streamlined design, flexible windows for essential data, remote assessments where possible, removal of non-essential activities, and review of prohibited medications so brief use without effect on assessments does not exclude.

R4-063.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-063.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-063.paraphrase: Sponsors should seek input from stakeholders such as potential participants, investigators and site staff so that protocol procedures are feasible and not unduly burdensome.

R4-064.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-064.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-064.paraphrase: Before or during protocol development, sponsors should run a risk assessment to find elements (visit structure, procedures, windows, enrolment criteria) that can be made more flexible or removed, and should identify and document the elements critical to safety and data quality, such as enrolment criteria, safety monitoring and primary or secondary efficacy endpoint procedures.

R4-065.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-065.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-065.paraphrase: Sponsors should assess the risk that critical elements are not conducted correctly, mitigate those risks, and develop study-specific plans to minimise occurrence and impact of important deviations, e.g. medical monitoring plan, safety monitoring plan, data management plan, risk-based monitoring plan, independent endpoint adjudication charter (footnotes cite FDA-RBM13, FDA-RBM23 and ICH E6(R2)).
R4-065.record: medical monitoring plan, safety monitoring plan, data management plan, risk-based monitoring plan, endpoint adjudication charter

R4-066.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-066.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-066.paraphrase: Investigators, site staff, study monitors and sponsor staff should be trained to focus on critical elements, carry them out as specified and avoid important deviations.
R4-066.party: investigators, site staff, study monitors, and sponsor staff (to be trained)

R4-067.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-067.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-067.paraphrase: Site monitors and centralized monitoring should focus on critical elements to detect important deviations early, whether at particular sites or as patterns pointing to a systemic problem.

R4-068.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-068.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-068.paraphrase: For recurrent, similar deviations the sponsor or the clinical investigator should conduct a root-cause analysis to decide on appropriate actions and prevent recurrence.

R4-069.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-069.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-069.paraphrase: Sponsors should document the root-cause determination and any further action, such as a CAPA plan, an update of the risk assessment and mitigation plans, or a protocol amendment, and should consider updating their analysis if the deviations affect critical-to-quality factors.
R4-069.record: RCA documentation; CAPA plan; updated risk assessment; protocol amendment
verify_notes: FDA draft guidance asks sponsors to consider updating 'their analysis' if deviations affect critical-to-quality factors; it does not say whether root cause or statistical analysis.
verify_raw: 'updating their analysis' (lines 324-325) does not say which analysis is meant (root-cause or statistical analysis)

R4-070.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-070.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-070.paraphrase: A high number of deviations at a site may signal that more resources, such as staffing or training, are needed.

R4-071.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, nonbinding); binding minimum is 21CFR312.56(b) (secure compliance or end participation); EU: not applicable
R4-071.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-071.paraphrase: Sponsors should consider closing a trial site that, despite remediation, cannot maintain GCP standards, follow the protocol or resolve recurring important deviations.

R4-072.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, nonbinding); IRB reporting procedures binding under 21CFR56.108; investigator IRB reporting binding under 21CFR312.66 for changes and unanticipated problems; EU: not applicable
R4-072.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-072.paraphrase: Where possible, FDA recommends that the investigator submit important protocol deviations to the IRB when they are identified, following the IRB's written procedures.

R4-073.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-073.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-073.paraphrase: The IRB should review important deviations submitted by investigators as soon as possible to determine their effect on participant safety or study conduct.

R4-074.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-074.deadline: not immediately; no period stated (IRB procedures decide)
R4-074.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-074.paraphrase: Deviations not classified as important and posing no apparent immediate hazard need not be reported to the IRB immediately.

R4-075.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, nonbinding); underlying approval rules binding under 21CFR312.30 and 21CFR312.66; EU: not applicable
R4-075.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-075.paraphrase: Protocol changes are generally not implemented until IRB review and approval and, in some cases, FDA review; changes to protocol-specified procedures made without prior IRB approval and without submitting the implementing amendment to FDA are protocol deviations.

R4-076.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, for comment, nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-076.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-076.paraphrase: Sponsors and clinical investigators are encouraged to engage IRBs as early as possible when urgent or emergent changes to the protocol or informed consent are anticipated.

R4-077.binding_route: US: FDA draft guidance (Level 1, nonbinding) for treating it as a deviation; the immediate-hazard exception itself is binding under 21CFR312.30(b)(2)(ii) and 21CFR312.66; EU: not applicable
R4-077.deadline: per SIII.B routes (sponsor timeframe; IRB when identified for important deviations)
R4-077.doc: Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices - Draft Guidance for Industry, December 2024 (CDER, CBER, CDRH, OCE; docket FDA-2023-D-5016)
R4-077.paraphrase: Changes needed to minimise or eliminate immediate hazards or to protect participants' life and well-being may be implemented without prior IRB approval or before the IND amendment (312.30(b)(2)(ii)), but such a change made before IRB approval is still a protocol deviation and should be reported as one (per SIII.B).
R4-077.party: not named (reporting per SIII.B: investigator to sponsor and IRB)

R4-080.binding_route: US: FDA final guidance (nonbinding recommendations); supports binding sponsor monitoring duty in 21CFR312.50 / 312.56(a); EU: not applicable
R4-080.doc: Oversight of Clinical Investigations - A Risk-Based Approach to Monitoring, Guidance for Industry, August 2013 (final; docket FDA-2011-D-0597)
R4-080.paraphrase: Sponsors should prospectively identify critical data and processes whose errors would threaten subject protection or trial integrity; examples include verifying that informed consent was properly obtained, adherence to eligibility criteria, investigational product accountability and administration, endpoint and protocol-required safety assessments, serious adverse event reporting, and blinding and allocation concealment.

R4-081.binding_route: US: FDA final guidance (nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-081.doc: Oversight of Clinical Investigations - A Risk-Based Approach to Monitoring, Guidance for Industry, August 2013 (final; docket FDA-2011-D-0597)
R4-081.paraphrase: The risk assessment should focus on risks to critical data and processes and rank them by likelihood of error, impact on subject protection and trial integrity, and detectability; results inform the monitoring plan, and sponsors may decide some risks are better handled outside monitoring, e.g. by modifying the protocol to remove the source of risk.

R4-082.binding_route: US: FDA final guidance (nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-082.doc: Oversight of Clinical Investigations - A Risk-Based Approach to Monitoring, Guidance for Industry, August 2013 (final; docket FDA-2011-D-0597)
R4-082.paraphrase: Centralized monitoring should be used where appropriate; routine review of submitted data can identify missing, inconsistent or outlying data and potential protocol deviations that may indicate systemic or significant errors, and sponsors should analyse site characteristics and performance metrics to find sites associated with poor performance or noncompliance.

R4-083.binding_route: US: FDA final guidance (nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-083.doc: Oversight of Clinical Investigations - A Risk-Based Approach to Monitoring, Guidance for Industry, August 2013 (final; docket FDA-2011-D-0597)
R4-083.paraphrase: If an investigator differs markedly from others in metrics such as the number of protocol deviations, the site should be considered for targeted on-site visits; sponsors may set up a mechanism to track deviations affecting data needed to interpret the primary endpoint and to notify key study personnel.

R4-084.binding_route: US: FDA final guidance (nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-084.doc: Oversight of Clinical Investigations - A Risk-Based Approach to Monitoring, Guidance for Industry, August 2013 (final; docket FDA-2011-D-0597)
R4-084.paraphrase: The monitoring plan should identify possible deviations or failures critical to study integrity and state how they are to be recorded and reported.
verify_raw: Sub-section (IV.D.1 vs IV.D.2) and printed page of the sentence on recording and reporting critical deviations differ between fetches

R4-085.binding_route: US: FDA final guidance (nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-085.doc: Oversight of Clinical Investigations - A Risk-Based Approach to Monitoring, Guidance for Industry, August 2013 (final; docket FDA-2011-D-0597)
R4-085.paraphrase: Among possible monitoring plan components, the communication part might cover the format, content, timing and archiving of monitoring reports and the immediate reporting of significant monitoring issues to appropriate parties, such as sponsor management, investigators and site staff, the IRB and FDA as necessary.
verify_raw: Printed page of IV.D.2 passage (TOC says 15; fetches gave 16 and 17)

R4-086.binding_route: US: FDA final guidance (nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-086.doc: Oversight of Clinical Investigations - A Risk-Based Approach to Monitoring, Guidance for Industry, August 2013 (final; docket FDA-2011-D-0597)
R4-086.paraphrase: Monitoring plan components might include how unresolved or significant noncompliance (e.g. serious protocol noncompliance, suspected data falsification) is handled at one or several sites, processes ensuring root-cause analysis where important deviations are found and appropriate corrective and preventive action such as additional training, and references to other quality management procedures.

R4-087.binding_route: US: FDA final guidance (nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-087.doc: Oversight of Clinical Investigations - A Risk-Based Approach to Monitoring, Guidance for Industry, August 2013 (final; docket FDA-2011-D-0597)
R4-087.paraphrase: Sponsors should consider which events would call for reviewing and revising the monitoring plan, e.g. a protocol amendment, a change in the definition of significant protocol deviations, or newly identified risks to study integrity.

R4-088.binding_route: US: FDA final guidance (nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-088.doc: Oversight of Clinical Investigations - A Risk-Based Approach to Monitoring, Guidance for Industry, August 2013 (final; docket FDA-2011-D-0597)
R4-088.paraphrase: Monitoring documentation should generally record the date and people involved, a summary of data or activities reviewed, any noncompliance, potential noncompliance, data irregularities or other deficiencies, and actions taken, planned or recommended with the responsible person and expected completion date; it should reach appropriate management in a timely way for review and follow-up.

R4-089.binding_route: US: FDA final guidance (nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-089.doc: A Risk-Based Approach to Monitoring of Clinical Investigations - Questions and Answers, Guidance for Industry, April 2023 (final; docket FDA-2019-D-0362)
R4-089.paraphrase: Sponsors should document their risk assessment (methods, conclusions and how it informed risk management) and reassess as issues arise; FDA may request the initial and updated assessments during inspection.

R4-090.binding_route: US: FDA final guidance (nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-090.doc: A Risk-Based Approach to Monitoring of Clinical Investigations - Questions and Answers, Guidance for Industry, April 2023 (final; docket FDA-2019-D-0362)
R4-090.paraphrase: Sponsors should monitor the important and likely risks from the initial assessment, watch for unanticipated risks affecting critical processes or data, and revise monitoring plans when new risk information emerges.

R4-091.binding_route: US: FDA final guidance (nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-091.doc: A Risk-Based Approach to Monitoring of Clinical Investigations - Questions and Answers, Guidance for Industry, April 2023 (final; docket FDA-2019-D-0362)
R4-091.paraphrase: An early monitoring visit may help sponsors detect protocol deviations and other issues sooner so corrective actions can begin earlier; source data verification should follow the risk assessment and focus on critical data and processes.

R4-092.binding_route: US: FDA final guidance (nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-092.doc: A Risk-Based Approach to Monitoring of Clinical Investigations - Questions and Answers, Guidance for Industry, April 2023 (final; docket FDA-2019-D-0362)
R4-092.paraphrase: Where centralized monitoring shows repeated issues at a site, such as delayed or missing assessments, the sponsor should promptly determine whether a site visit and corrective actions are needed.

R4-093.binding_route: US: FDA final guidance (nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-093.doc: A Risk-Based Approach to Monitoring of Clinical Investigations - Questions and Answers, Guidance for Industry, April 2023 (final; docket FDA-2019-D-0362)
R4-093.paraphrase: Blinding should be treated as a critical process; deviations that could cause unintended unblinding should be identified, tracked and considered part of the monitoring plan.

R4-094.binding_route: US: FDA final guidance (nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-094.doc: A Risk-Based Approach to Monitoring of Clinical Investigations - Questions and Answers, Guidance for Industry, April 2023 (final; docket FDA-2019-D-0362)
R4-094.paraphrase: FDA recommends that monitoring plans, built on the trial's risk assessment, include among other components the types of issues found through monitoring that trigger immediate escalation, and an approach to check whether issues found at one site exist at others or signal systemic protocol problems; other plans may be referenced.

R4-095.binding_route: US: FDA final guidance (nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-095.doc: A Risk-Based Approach to Monitoring of Clinical Investigations - Questions and Answers, Guidance for Industry, April 2023 (final; docket FDA-2019-D-0362)
R4-095.paraphrase: Significant issues found through monitoring should be evaluated promptly at the appropriate levels; root-cause analysis and corrective and preventive action should be undertaken promptly, the risk assessment and monitoring plan reviewed and revised, and the protocol amended where corrective actions change processes; example actions are retraining, halting enrolment at a site, clarifying the protocol and changing vendor agreements.
R4-095.record: RCA; CAPA; revised risk assessment and monitoring plan; protocol amendment

R4-096.binding_route: US: FDA final guidance (nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-096.doc: A Risk-Based Approach to Monitoring of Clinical Investigations - Questions and Answers, Guidance for Industry, April 2023 (final; docket FDA-2019-D-0362)
R4-096.paraphrase: Significant issues and the actions taken should be documented and communicated to relevant parties, which may include sponsor management and teams, clinical sites, IRBs, data monitoring committees, relevant contract research organisations and regulators, including FDA when appropriate.

R4-097.binding_route: US: FDA final guidance (nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-097.doc: A Risk-Based Approach to Monitoring of Clinical Investigations - Questions and Answers, Guidance for Industry, April 2023 (final; docket FDA-2019-D-0362)
R4-097.paraphrase: Monitoring documentation (on-site, remote and centralized) should generally record activity date, participants, data reviewed, noncompliance or irregularities and actions taken or recommended, in enough detail to verify adherence to the monitoring plan, and should be provided promptly to appropriate management.

R4-098.binding_route: US: FDA final guidance (nonbinding recommendations); EU: not applicable
R4-098.doc: A Risk-Based Approach to Monitoring of Clinical Investigations - Questions and Answers, Guidance for Industry, April 2023 (final; docket FDA-2019-D-0362)

R5-047.paraphrase: For each important deviation, the impact on the data sets and populations defined in the statistical analysis plan is assessed.

R5-048.binding_route: EU: none (industry best practice); US: none (industry best practice)

R5-048.paraphrase: At protocol design, consideration of critical to quality factors is foundational to building quality into the trial; in parallel, sponsors should define risk management strategies (integrated quality risk management plans enabling a risk-based monitoring strategy), including controls such as QTLs and key risk indicators.
R5-048.quote: at the time of protocol design, CtQ consideration is foundational

R5-049.binding_route: EU: none (industry best practice); US: none (industry best practice)
R5-049.doc: Quality Tolerance Limits: Framework for Successful Implementation in Clinical Development. Therapeutic Innovation and Regulatory Science 55(2):251-261, 2021 (online 3 Sep 2020; TransCelerate working group, CC BY 4.0)
R5-049.paraphrase: QTLs are an added control for risks to critical to quality factors; their number should match the protocol's risk level, stay limited, and ideally align with the CtQ factors.

R5-050.binding_route: EU: none (industry best practice); US: none (industry best practice)
R5-050.doc: Quality Tolerance Limits: Framework for Successful Implementation in Clinical Development. Therapeutic Innovation and Regulatory Science 55(2):251-261, 2021 (online 3 Sep 2020; TransCelerate working group, CC BY 4.0)
R5-050.paraphrase: QTLs are trial-level indicators and KRIs are site- or country-level; they can share a parameter, e.g. the proportion of participants with eligibility-criteria protocol deviations, or premature discontinuation. A trial-level QTL exceedance is expected to show as similar KRI signals across several sites or countries; either needs evaluation and mitigation at the right level.

R5-051.binding_route: EU: none (industry best practice); US: none (industry best practice)
R5-051.doc: Quality Tolerance Limits: Framework for Successful Implementation in Clinical Development. Therapeutic Innovation and Regulatory Science 55(2):251-261, 2021 (online 3 Sep 2020; TransCelerate working group, CC BY 4.0)
R5-051.paraphrase: In the Define stage, the QTL monitoring approach sets the action plan for a deviation from a predefined QTL threshold, criteria for judging how important such a deviation is, and actions if important ones occur. Here 'deviation' means a QTL threshold exceedance, not a protocol deviation.

R5-052.binding_route: EU: none (industry best practice); US: none (industry best practice)
R5-052.doc: Quality Tolerance Limits: Framework for Successful Implementation in Clinical Development. Therapeutic Innovation and Regulatory Science 55(2):251-261, 2021 (online 3 Sep 2020; TransCelerate working group, CC BY 4.0)
R5-052.paraphrase: For important QTL deviations that may affect participant safety or reliability of results, issue management may include root cause analysis and corrective or preventive actions; for unimportant ones, operational changes within the protocol or a revised QTL definition or threshold may follow. Early (secondary) limits allow action before a QTL is breached.

R5-053.binding_route: EU: none (industry best practice; CSR duty itself from ICH E6, R1); US: none
R5-053.doc: Quality Tolerance Limits: Framework for Successful Implementation in Clinical Development. Therapeutic Innovation and Regulatory Science 55(2):251-261, 2021 (online 3 Sep 2020; TransCelerate working group, CC BY 4.0)
R5-053.paraphrase: In the Report stage all QTL deviations of the trial are reviewed (a QTL summary report lists them with actions taken) and the CSR summarises the quality management approach, the important QTL deviations and the actions taken.

R5-054.binding_route: EU: none (industry best practice); US: none (industry best practice)
R5-054.doc: Quality Tolerance Limits: Framework for Successful Implementation in Clinical Development. Therapeutic Innovation and Regulatory Science 55(2):251-261, 2021 (online 3 Sep 2020; TransCelerate working group, CC BY 4.0)
R5-054.paraphrase: The sponsor keeps accountability for the QTL process even when activities are outsourced; the work is cross-functional (e.g. clinical development, biostatistics, medical monitoring, pharmacovigilance).
